19.b: Chicken provides protein; the lettuce adds fiber and vitamins; Parmesan provides calcium.
19.a: Gluten (croutons), milk, eggs; fish if the dressing contains anchovies; possibly mustard.
s: Prepare the ingredients: take the chicken breast (250 g) out of the fridge 15 minutes ahead, pat it dry and season it with salt and pepper. Wash the romaine lettuce (150 g), dry it well and tear it into 3-4 cm pieces. Grate the 30 g of Parmesan. Measure out 60 g of croutons and 60 g of Caesar dressing. Set out a skillet and a large bowl.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat with a little oil. Add the chicken breast and cook it for 6-7 minutes on one side, until browned.

Flip the breast, lower the heat to medium and cook for another 6-7 minutes, until the meat is cooked through and, when cut at the thickest point, nothing pink remains (75°C inside). Tip: slice a very thick breast in half horizontally so it cooks evenly.
Transfer the chicken to a plate and let it rest for 5 minutes. Then slice it diagonally into 1 cm slices.

Put the lettuce in the bowl, add the 60 g of Caesar dressing and toss gently until the leaves are evenly coated. Tip: toss the dressing with the lettuce right before serving, so the leaves stay crisp.
Divide the salad between 2 bowls. Top with the croutons, the sliced chicken and the grated Parmesan. Serve immediately; the cooked chicken keeps separately in the fridge for 2 days.

20.b: Tuna provides protein and omega-3 fatty acids; the vegetables add fiber and vitamins.
s: Prepare the ingredients: open the can and drain the 160 g of tuna well, then flake it into pieces with a fork. Drain the 100 g of sweetcorn. Wash the tomatoes (120 g), cucumbers (100 g) and lettuce (80 g). Set out a large bowl.
Cut the tomatoes into 2 cm pieces and the cucumbers into rounds or 1 cm cubes. Tear the lettuce into small pieces by hand.
Put the lettuce in the bowl, then add the tomatoes, cucumbers and sweetcorn. Spread the tuna on top.
Drizzle with the 15 ml of olive oil and the juice of half a lemon, and add salt and pepper to taste. Tip: squeeze the lemon in gradually and taste, so the salad doesn't turn out too sour.
Toss gently so the tuna doesn't break up too much. Serve immediately; it keeps in the fridge for 1 day, but the leaves will wilt.

21.b: Avocado provides fiber, potassium, vitamin E and monounsaturated fats.
21.a: The basic recipe contains none of the major allergens; check any added ingredients.
s: Wash the tomatoes (200 g), peel the red onion (50 g) and wash the herbs. Cut the tomatoes into 1.5 cm cubes. Cut the onion into very thin rings or small dice. Chop the herbs finely. Set out a bowl.
Cut the avocado in half, remove the pit and scoop out the flesh with a spoon. Cut the flesh into 1.5 cm cubes. Tip: choose a ripe avocado that gives slightly when pressed.
Put the avocado in the bowl right away and drizzle it with the 15 ml of lemon juice so it doesn't turn brown.
Add the tomatoes, onion and herbs, then the 10 ml of olive oil, salt and pepper. Toss gently with 3-4 motions from the bottom up, so the avocado doesn't turn to mush.
Serve immediately, cold. If you need to store it, cover it with plastic wrap pressed against the surface and keep it in the fridge for no more than a few hours.

22.b: Carbohydrates for energy, fiber from the vegetables and calcium from the mozzarella.
22.a: Gluten and milk; possibly eggs in the pasta and soy/sesame in packaged products.
s: Prepare the ingredients: measure out 250 g of pasta, 30 ml of olive oil and 80 g of drained sweetcorn. Wash the cherry tomatoes (150 g) and cut them in half. Wash the cucumbers (100 g) and cut them into 1 cm cubes. Drain the mozzarella (100 g) and cut it into 1 cm cubes. Wash the basil and tear the leaves. Put 2 liters of water in a large pot.
Bring the water to a boil over high heat and add a tablespoon of salt. When it boils, add the pasta and stir.

Cook the pasta according to the package directions, about 9-11 minutes, until tender but firm (al dente). Tip: for a salad, cook the pasta one minute less than the package says, so it doesn't turn soft when tossed.
Drain the pasta and quickly rinse it under cold water for 30 seconds to stop the cooking and cool it down. Drain it well and put it in a large bowl.
Add the cherry tomatoes, cucumbers, sweetcorn and mozzarella to the bowl.
Add the 30 ml of olive oil, the basil, salt and pepper. Toss gently until all the ingredients are coated with oil.
Serve immediately or chill the salad in the fridge for 15 minutes. Store in the fridge, in an airtight container, for 2 days.

23.b: Eggs provide protein and choline; the dairy contributes calcium and protein.
23.a: Eggs and milk; the cheese may contain milk.
s: Prepare the ingredients: crack the 4 eggs into a bowl. Grate or finely chop the 60 g of cheese. Wash the tomatoes (100 g) and cut them into 5 mm slices. Set out a 20-24 cm nonstick skillet and a spatula.

Add the 30 ml of milk, salt and pepper to the eggs and beat them with a fork or whisk for 30 seconds, until the mixture is smooth and slightly frothy. Tip: don't beat too much, so the omelet doesn't turn out dry.
Set the skillet over low-medium heat and add the 5 ml of oil, spreading it with a paper towel. Wait 30 seconds for it to warm up.
Pour the eggs into the skillet. Leave them for 1 minute, then gently pull the edges toward the center with the spatula, letting the liquid part flow out to the edges.
When the omelet is almost set but still a little glossy on top, after about 2-3 minutes, sprinkle the cheese over half of the surface.
Fold the omelet in half with the spatula and cook for another 30-60 seconds, until the cheese melts and the eggs are completely set, with no liquid parts.
Slide the omelet onto a plate and serve immediately with the tomato slices alongside. Eat it fresh.

24.b: Avocado provides fiber and unsaturated fats; eggs provide protein.
24.a: Gluten and eggs; the bread may contain sesame or soy.
s: Prepare the ingredients: cut the avocado in half, remove the pit and scoop the flesh into a bowl with a spoon. Have the lemon juice (10 ml) and pepper ready. Set out a nonstick skillet, a fork and a toaster or a pan for toasting the bread.
Toast the 2 slices of bread in the toaster or in a dry skillet, 2 minutes on each side, until golden and crisp.
Mash the avocado with a fork until you have a paste with small chunks. Add the 10 ml of lemon juice, salt and pepper and mix. Tip: keep a bit of texture; the paste shouldn't be completely smooth.
Spread a thick layer of avocado paste on each slice of warm toast.

Heat a skillet over medium heat with a little oil or butter and crack in the 2 eggs. Fry them for 2-3 minutes, until the white is completely set and the yolk is still runny; for a firmer yolk, cook for another 1-2 minutes. Tip: for safety, the egg should be well cooked, with no liquid white.
Place an egg on top of each toast. Sprinkle with freshly ground pepper and serve immediately.

25.b: Oats contain beta-glucans and fiber; the fruit provides vitamins and antioxidants.
25.a: Milk; oats may be contaminated with gluten; honey is not vegan.
s: Prepare the ingredients: measure out 100 g of rolled oats and 300 ml of milk. Peel the banana (120 g) and cut it into 5 mm rounds. Wash the berries (100 g) and dry them. Set out a small 1-liter saucepan and a wooden spoon.
Put the oats and the 300 ml of milk in the saucepan. Add a pinch of salt.
Set the saucepan over medium heat and bring the milk almost to a boil, stirring occasionally, for 2-3 minutes.

Lower the heat to low and simmer for 5-7 minutes, stirring often, until the porridge thickens and the oats are soft. If it gets too thick, add 2-3 tablespoons of water or milk. Tip: stir constantly so the porridge doesn't stick to the bottom of the saucepan.
Take the saucepan off the heat and let the porridge rest for 1-2 minutes. Divide the porridge between 2 bowls.
Top with the banana, the berries and, if you like, the 10 g of honey. Serve warm. For a vegan version, use plant-based milk and leave out the honey.

26.b: Yogurt provides protein and calcium; the fruit and oats contribute fiber.
26.a: Milk; granola may contain gluten, tree nuts, peanuts, sesame or soy.
s: Prepare the ingredients: measure out 300 g of yogurt, 80 g of granola and 150 g of berries. Wash the berries and pat them lightly dry. Set out 2 bowls or tall glasses.
Divide the yogurt between the 2 bowls or glasses, 150 g each, and smooth the surface with the back of a spoon.
Add the granola on top, 40 g to each bowl. Tip: add the granola right before serving, so it stays crunchy.
Add the berries and, if you like, the 10 g of honey in a thin stream. For a vegan version, use plant-based yogurt and leave out the honey.
Serve immediately. If you are preparing the portions ahead of time, keep the granola separate.

27.b: Protein from the ham and cheese, calcium from the cheese and vitamins from the vegetables.
27.a: Gluten, milk; possibly mustard, soy and sesame, depending on the bread, ham and spread.
s: Prepare the ingredients: wash the tomatoes (80 g) and lettuce (30 g) and dry them. Cut the tomatoes into 5 mm slices. Cut the cheese (60 g) into thin slices. Set out the 4 slices of bread (160 g), the mustard (10 g), if using, and a plate.
Lay 2 slices of bread on the plate. If you like, spread a thin layer of mustard on each with a knife.
Add the lettuce leaves to each slice, then the tomato slices, and sprinkle with a little salt. Tip: put the lettuce directly on the bread, so the tomatoes don't make it soggy.
Add the 80 g of ham and the cheese slices, dividing them equally between the 2 sandwiches.

Top with the other 2 slices of bread and press down lightly. Cut the sandwiches in half diagonally and serve immediately. If you make it ahead, wrap it in foil and keep it in the fridge for no more than 1 day.

69.b: Chickpeas and spinach provide plant protein, iron and folate.
69.a: No major allergens in the base ingredients; check the labels of the products you use.
s: Prepare the ingredients: drain and rinse 480 g of cooked chickpeas, peel 100 g of onion and cut it into 0.5 cm dice, peel 2 garlic cloves and mince them finely, peel 10 g of ginger and grate it finely, and wash 150 g of spinach and drain it well. Take out a 24–26 cm saucepan or deep frying pan and a wooden spoon, and measure out 15 ml of oil, 10 g of curry powder, 200 ml of coconut milk and 400 g of diced tomatoes.
Heat the 15 ml of oil in the pan over medium heat for 1 minute, until the oil moves easily across the base. Add the onion and sauté for 4–5 minutes, stirring often, until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir for 30–40 seconds, until fragrant, without letting them brown. Tip: if the garlic sticks to the bottom, add 2 tablespoons of water and stir.
Sprinkle the 10 g of curry powder over the onion and stir for 30 seconds over low heat so the spices release their aroma, then immediately deglaze with the tomatoes.

Pour in the 400 g of diced tomatoes, then the 200 ml of coconut milk, and stir well, scraping the bottom of the pan. Bring the sauce to a simmer over medium heat, until small bubbles appear around the edges.

Add the drained chickpeas, reduce the heat to low and simmer for 15 minutes, uncovered or with the lid slightly ajar, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens slightly to the consistency of a thick soup.
Add the spinach to the pan in 2–3 batches and stir for 2–3 minutes, until it wilts and reduces in volume. Taste and adjust the salt. Tip: if the sauce is too thick, add 50 ml of hot water.
Serve the curry hot in deep bowls, divided into 4 equal portions. It goes very well with cooked rice or bread.

70.n: Mămăligă (polenta) with cheese and sour cream
70.b: Cornmeal provides energy; the cheese and sour cream provide protein and calcium.
70.a: Contains: Milk. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Prepare the ingredients: measure 250 g of cornmeal into a bowl, 1 litre of water and a level teaspoon of salt (about 5 g). Take out a heavy-bottomed 3-litre pot, a long-handled wooden spoon and a whisk or large spoon, crumble the telemea (200 g) with a fork into a bowl, and put the sour cream (200 g) in another bowl.
Put the 1000 ml of water in the pot, add the salt and heat over high heat until the water boils vigorously, with large bubbles.

Reduce the heat to medium and pour in the cornmeal in a steady rain, a little at a time through your fingers, stirring constantly with the whisk or spoon so that no lumps form. This takes about 2 minutes. Tip: if lumps do form, crush them with the back of the spoon.

Reduce the heat to low and cook the mămăligă for 25–30 minutes, stirring often with the wooden spoon, especially along the bottom of the pot, so it does not stick. The mămăligă is ready when it pulls away easily from the sides of the pot and is thick and creamy.
If the mămăligă thickens too quickly, add 2–3 tablespoons of hot water and stir. If you want it to come out firm enough to turn out, cook it for another 3–4 minutes, stirring vigorously.
Take the pot off the heat and let the mămăligă rest for 3 minutes, then turn it out onto a wooden board and cut it into slices with a piece of thread or string.
Serve the mămăligă hot on 4 plates, topped with the crumbled cheese and the sour cream while it is still steaming.

71.b: Mackerel: omega-3, vitamin D and protein.
71.a: Contains: Fish. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Prepare the ingredients: wash 300 g of potatoes well and cut them into slices about 0.5 cm thick, peel 100 g of onion and cut it into thin rings, and rinse the 500 g of mackerel and pat it dry with paper towels. Preheat the oven to 200°C with the rack in the middle position, and grease a roughly 25 x 30 cm baking tray with 10 ml of oil.
Arrange the potato slices in an even layer in the tray, then cover them with the onion rings. Drizzle another 10 ml of oil over the top and sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Bake the potatoes and onion on their own for 10 minutes at 200°C so they begin to soften, since potatoes need longer than the fish.

Meanwhile, season the mackerel with salt and pepper, inside and out, and rub it with the remaining 10 ml of oil. Tip: if the mackerel is whole, make 2–3 diagonal slashes on each side so it cooks evenly.
Take the tray out of the oven, place the fish on top of the potatoes and sprinkle it with 15 ml of lemon juice.

Return the tray to the oven and bake for another 25–30 minutes (35–40 minutes in total), until the fish skin is golden and the flesh flakes easily when pressed with a fork, and the potatoes are tender when pierced.
Take out the tray and let everything rest for 3 minutes. Serve the mackerel with the potatoes and onion on 2 plates, drizzled with the juices from the tray.

72.b: Energy from the rice, plus fibre and vitamins from the vegetables.
72.a: No major allergens in the base ingredients; check the labels of the products you use.
s: Prepare the ingredients: rinse 250 g of rice in a sieve under cold running water until the water runs almost clear. Peel 100 g of carrot and cut it into 0.5 cm dice, peel 80 g of onion and chop it finely, and drain 100 g of peas if they are canned. Measure out 20 ml of oil, 500 ml of water and some salt. Take out a 2-litre saucepan with a lid.
Heat the 20 ml of oil in the saucepan over medium heat for 1 minute. Add the onion and carrot and sauté for 4–5 minutes, stirring, until the onion is translucent and the carrot is slightly softened.
Add the drained rice and stir for 1–2 minutes, until the grains become slightly translucent at the edges and are coated in oil. Tip: this step helps the grains stay separate and fluffy.
Add the peas, the 500 ml of water and a teaspoon of salt (about 5 g). Stir just once and bring to a boil over high heat.
When the water starts to boil, reduce the heat to low, cover with the lid and cook for 15 minutes, without lifting the lid and without stirring, until the rice has absorbed all the water.
Take the pan off the heat, leave it covered for 5 minutes to let the rice rest, then fluff it gently with a fork. Taste and adjust the salt.
Serve the vegetable rice warm, in 4 equal portions, as a side dish or a light main course.

73.b: Potatoes provide potassium, vitamin C and B6.
73.a: No major allergens in the base ingredients; check the labels of the products you use.
s: Prepare the ingredients: preheat the oven to 210°C with the rack in the middle position. Wash 800 g of potatoes well (there is no need to peel them if they are new potatoes) and cut them into pieces of about 3 cm. Peel 4 garlic cloves and gently crush them with the flat of a knife blade, or leave them whole in their skins. Prepare a large 30 x 40 cm baking tray.
Pat the cut potatoes dry with a clean towel so they are not wet, otherwise they will not brown. Tip: for crispier potatoes, soak them in cold water for 5 minutes before cutting and dry them well.

Put the potatoes in a large bowl and add 30 ml of oil, the rosemary (about 2 sprigs, or 1 tablespoon chopped), the garlic and a teaspoon of salt (5 g). Toss with your hands until all the pieces are evenly coated.
Tip the potatoes into the tray and spread them in a single layer with space between them, so they brown instead of steaming.
Bake for 20 minutes at 210°C, then take out the tray and turn the potatoes with a spatula.
Return the tray to the oven and bake for another 20–25 minutes (40–45 minutes in total), until the potatoes are golden and crisp on the outside and tender when pierced with a fork.
Take the potatoes out of the oven and serve immediately, in 4 portions, as a side dish for meat, fish or salad.

74.a: Contains: Milk. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Prepare the ingredients: peel 800 g of potatoes with a vegetable peeler and cut them into equal pieces of about 3–4 cm so they cook evenly. Measure out 150 ml of milk and 40 g of butter (cut into cubes), and take out a 3-litre pot, a colander and a potato masher.
Put the potatoes in the pot, cover them with cold water by about 2 cm and add a teaspoon of salt (5 g). Bring to a boil over high heat.
When the water boils, reduce the heat to medium and cook the potatoes for 15–20 minutes, until completely soft and a fork slides in easily, with no resistance.

While the potatoes cook, warm the 150 ml of milk in a small saucepan over low heat for 2–3 minutes, until warm but not boiling. Tip: warm milk makes the mash creamier and prevents it from turning lumpy.
Drain the potatoes well in the colander and return them to the warm pot, off the heat, for 1 minute to let the excess moisture evaporate.
Mash the hot potatoes with the masher until no lumps remain. Add the butter and stir until completely melted.
Pour in the warm milk gradually, stirring vigorously with a wooden spoon, until you get a smooth, creamy mash. Add a pinch of grated nutmeg (about 1 g) and salt to taste.
Serve the mash immediately while warm, in 4 portions, as a side dish for meat or vegetables.

75.b: Lower in fat than fries and rich in potassium.
75.a: No major allergens in the base ingredients; check the labels of the products you use.
s: Prepare the ingredients: preheat the oven to 220°C with the rack in the middle position. Wash 800 g of potatoes well (you can leave the skin on) and cut them into thick wedges about 1.5 cm wide, long and spear-shaped. Measure out 30 ml of oil, 5 g of sweet paprika, 5 g of smoked paprika and a teaspoon of salt (5 g). Prepare a large tray lined with baking paper.
Pat the potato wedges dry with a kitchen towel. Tip: dry potatoes brown better and turn out crispier.
Put the potatoes in a large bowl, add the oil and toss with your hands until all the pieces are glossy.
Sprinkle the sweet paprika, smoked paprika and salt over the potatoes and toss again until the spices evenly coat every wedge.
Arrange the potatoes on the tray, cut side down, in a single layer with a little space between them.
Bake for 15 minutes at 220°C, then turn the wedges with a spatula and bake for another 15–20 minutes (30–35 minutes in total), until golden on the outside and tender when pierced with a fork.
Take out the tray, let the potatoes rest for 2 minutes and serve hot in 4 portions, as a side dish or snack.

76.b: Rich in vitamin A (beta-carotene) and fibre.
76.a: No major allergens in the base ingredients; check the labels of the products you use.
s: Prepare the ingredients: preheat the oven to 210°C with the rack in the middle position. Wash and peel 800 g of sweet potatoes with a peeler, then cut them into cubes of about 2–3 cm. Measure out 30 ml of olive oil, a teaspoon of thyme (2 g) and a teaspoon of salt (5 g). Prepare a large tray lined with baking paper.
Put the sweet potato cubes in a large bowl and add the olive oil. Toss with your hands or a spoon until every cube is coated in oil.
Add the thyme and salt and toss again until the seasoning is evenly distributed. Tip: you can rub the dried thyme between your palms to release its aroma.
Tip the sweet potatoes onto the tray and spread them in a single layer with space between the cubes. If the tray is too crowded, use two trays so they do not steam.
Bake for 15 minutes at 210°C, then take out the tray and stir the sweet potatoes with a spatula.
Return the tray to the oven and bake for another 10–15 minutes (25–30 minutes in total), until the cubes are golden at the edges and tender when pierced with a fork.
Serve the sweet potatoes hot, in 4 portions, as a side dish or as the base for a vegetable bowl.

77.b: Fibre and vitamins A, C and K from a mix of vegetables.
77.a: No major allergens in the base ingredients; check the labels of the products you use.
s: Prepare the ingredients: preheat the oven to 200°C with the rack in the middle position. Wash the vegetables. Peel 200 g of carrot and cut it into 1 cm thick rounds, cut 200 g of zucchini into 1.5 cm half-moons, 200 g of bell pepper into 3 cm pieces, 150 g of red onion into 8 wedges and 200 g of cauliflower into 3–4 cm florets. Prepare a large 30 x 40 cm tray lined with baking paper.
Cut the vegetables into pieces that are as even as possible so they cook at the same time. Tip: carrots take longer to roast, so cut them thinner than the other vegetables.
Put all the vegetables in a large bowl and add 30 ml of olive oil, a teaspoon of thyme (2 g) and a teaspoon of salt (5 g).
Toss with your hands until all the vegetables are evenly coated in oil and seasoning.
Spread the vegetables on the tray in a single layer, without overlapping, so they brown nicely.
Bake for 15 minutes at 200°C, then take out the tray and stir the vegetables with a spatula.
Return the tray to the oven and bake for another 15–20 minutes (30–35 minutes in total), until the vegetables are golden at the edges and tender when pierced with a fork.
Serve the vegetables warm, in 4 portions, as a side dish or a vegetarian main course.

78.b: Broccoli provides vitamins C and K and folate.
78.a: No major allergens in the base ingredients; check the labels of the products you use.
s: Prepare the ingredients: wash 400 g of broccoli and cut it into 3–4 cm florets, and peel the 2 garlic cloves and slice them thinly. Measure out 15 ml of olive oil and 10 ml of lemon juice. Prepare a saucepan with 2–3 cm of water and a steamer basket (or a sieve that fits on top), plus a 24 cm frying pan.

Bring the water to a boil over high heat, then place the broccoli in the steamer basket, cover with a lid and steam for 5 minutes, until the florets turn bright green and are slightly tender when pierced with a fork but still crisp.
While the broccoli steams, heat the 15 ml of olive oil in the frying pan over low-medium heat for 1 minute.
Add the sliced garlic and brown it for 1–2 minutes, stirring, until lightly golden. Tip: do not let the garlic darken, because it turns bitter.
Add the steamed broccoli to the pan and stir for 1 minute so it is coated in the garlic oil.
Turn off the heat, add the 10 ml of lemon juice and a teaspoon of salt (3 g) to taste, and stir once.
Serve immediately, in 4 portions, as a warm side dish.

79.a: No major allergens in the base ingredients; check the labels of the products you use.
s: Prepare the ingredients: wash 500 g of green beans, trim the ends from both sides and, if the pods are long, cut them in half. Peel 3 garlic cloves and mince them. Measure out 20 ml of oil and 10 ml of lemon juice. Take out a 3-litre pot, a colander and a 26 cm frying pan.
Put 2 litres of water with a tablespoon of salt (15 g) in the pot and bring to a boil over high heat.
Add the green beans and boil for 8–10 minutes, until bright green and slightly tender when pierced with a fork, but still a little firm.
Drain the beans in the colander and, if you want to keep their vivid colour, quickly run them under cold water. Tip: drain them very well, otherwise they will spatter in the oil.
Heat the 20 ml of oil in the frying pan over medium heat for 1 minute. Add the garlic and sauté for 30 seconds, until fragrant, without letting it darken.
Add the drained beans to the pan and sauté for 3–4 minutes, stirring, until completely heated through and lightly browned in spots.
Turn off the heat, drizzle with the 10 ml of lemon juice and adjust the salt.
Serve immediately, in 4 portions, as a warm side dish.

80.b: Vitamins C and K, and fibre.
80.a: No major allergens in the base ingredients; check the labels of the products you use.
s: Prepare the ingredients: preheat the oven to 200°C with the rack in the middle position. Wash 600 g of cauliflower, remove the leaves and break it into 3–4 cm florets. Measure out 30 ml of oil, 5 g of turmeric, 5 g of cumin and a teaspoon of salt (5 g). Prepare a 30 x 40 cm tray lined with baking paper.
Dry the florets with a clean towel. Tip: dry cauliflower browns better and does not steam in the oven.
Put the cauliflower in a large bowl and add the oil, turmeric, cumin and salt. Toss with your hands until all the florets are evenly coated and have a yellow colour.
Tip the cauliflower onto the tray and spread it in a single layer with space between the florets.
Bake for 15 minutes at 200°C, then take out the tray and turn the florets with a spatula.
Return the tray to the oven and bake for another 10–15 minutes (25–30 minutes in total), until the cauliflower is golden at the edges and tender when pierced with a fork.
Serve the cauliflower warm, in 4 portions, as a side dish or snack.

81.b: Vitamins C and K, and fibre.
81.a: No major allergens in the base ingredients; check the labels of the products you use.
s: Prepare the ingredients: remove the outer leaves from 800 g of cabbage, cut out the core and slice it into thin strips of about 0.5 cm. Peel 100 g of onion and chop it finely. Measure out 30 ml of oil, 5 g of cumin, 100 ml of water and some salt. Take out a wide 3–4 litre pot with a lid.
Heat the 30 ml of oil in the pot over medium heat for 1 minute. Add the onion and sauté for 4–5 minutes, stirring, until translucent and lightly golden.
Add the cabbage to the pot in 2–3 batches, stirring after each, since the volume reduces as it wilts. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring often, until the cabbage begins to soften.
Add the cumin, the 100 ml of water and a teaspoon of salt (5 g). Stir well.

Cover the pot with the lid, reduce the heat to low and simmer for 25–30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the cabbage is soft, translucent and lightly golden. Tip: if it dries out too much, add 2–3 tablespoons of water.
Taste and adjust the salt. If there is still liquid, leave the lid off for another 2–3 minutes to let it evaporate.
Serve the braised cabbage warm, in 4 portions, as a side dish for meat or mămăligă.

82.b: Carbohydrates with fibre and vitamins from the vegetables.
82.a: Contains: Gluten. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Prepare the ingredients: measure 250 g of couscous into a heatproof bowl, 300 ml of water (put it on to boil) and 15 ml of oil. Wash 100 g of bell pepper and 100 g of carrot, peel the carrot and cut both vegetables into 0.5 cm dice. Wash and chop a handful of parsley (about 10 g) and measure out 15 ml of lemon juice.
Boil the 300 ml of water in a small saucepan or a kettle until it bubbles vigorously, then add half a teaspoon of salt (3 g).
Pour the hot water over the couscous, stir once with a fork, cover the bowl with a plate or cling film and leave for 5 minutes, until the couscous has absorbed all the water and swelled.
Uncover the bowl and fluff the couscous with a fork, using light motions, until the grains separate and it becomes light and fluffy. Tip: do not stir with a spoon, as it will turn sticky.
Add the bell pepper, carrot, oil and lemon juice to the couscous and toss gently until the vegetables are evenly distributed.
Add the chopped parsley and toss one last time. Taste and adjust the salt.
Serve the couscous warm or at room temperature, in 4 portions, as a side dish or a light main course.

83.b: Quinoa provides complete protein, iron and magnesium.
83.a: No major allergens in the base ingredients; check the labels of the products you use.
s: Prepare the ingredients: rinse 200 g of quinoa in a fine sieve under cold running water for 1 minute, rubbing the grains with your hand to remove the bitter coating. Wash and cut 100 g of bell pepper and 100 g of cucumber into 1 cm dice, halve 80 g of cherry tomatoes and chop a handful of parsley (10 g). Measure out 15 ml of olive oil and 15 ml of lemon juice.
Put the quinoa in a 2-litre saucepan, add 400 ml of water and half a teaspoon of salt (3 g) and bring to a boil over high heat.
Reduce the heat to low, cover with the lid and simmer for 12–15 minutes, until the water is absorbed, the grains are translucent and a small white ring (the germ) appears on each grain.
Take the pan off the heat and leave it covered for 5 minutes, then fluff the quinoa with a fork. Tip: do not lift the lid while it cooks, so the steam does not escape.
Spread the quinoa on a large plate or in a wide bowl and let it cool slightly for 5–10 minutes.
Add the bell pepper, cucumber, cherry tomatoes, olive oil and lemon juice to the quinoa, then toss gently.
Add the parsley, taste and adjust the salt. Serve the salad in 4 portions, warm or cold.

84.b: Vitamins A and C, and few calories.
84.a: Contains: Milk. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Prepare the ingredients: wash 800 g of pumpkin, cut it into slices, scoop out the seeds with a spoon and remove the skin with a sharp knife. Cut the flesh into 3 cm cubes. Measure out 20 g of butter, a teaspoon of salt (3 g) and a pinch of grated nutmeg (1 g). Take out a 3-litre pot and a hand blender or a masher.
Put the pumpkin in the pot, cover it with cold water until it only just reaches the level of the cubes and add a little salt. Bring to a boil over high heat.
Reduce the heat to medium and cook for 15–20 minutes, until the cubes are tender when pierced with a fork and mash easily. Alternatively, roast it on a tray at 200°C for 30–35 minutes.
Drain the pumpkin very well in a colander for 2–3 minutes, pressing lightly with a spoon. Tip: excess water makes the purée too runny.
Return the pumpkin to the warm pot and add the butter. Mash with the masher or hand blender until you have a smooth, creamy purée.
Add the nutmeg and salt, stir and taste, adjusting to your preference.
Serve the purée warm, in 4 portions, as a side dish for meat or on its own.

85.b: Light, with vitamins C and B6.
85.a: No major allergens in the base ingredients; check the labels of the products you use.
s: Prepare the ingredients: wash 600 g of zucchini, trim the ends and slice into rounds 1 cm thick. Peel 2 garlic cloves and mince them finely. Measure out 20 ml of olive oil, a teaspoon of dried oregano (2 g) and half a teaspoon of salt (3 g). Take out a large 28 cm frying pan.
Dry the zucchini rounds with a paper towel. Tip: if the zucchini is wet, it releases water and will not brown.
Heat the 20 ml of olive oil in the pan over medium-high heat for 1 minute, until the oil is hot.
Arrange the rounds in the pan in a single layer (cook in 2 batches if they do not all fit) and brown for 3–4 minutes on the first side, until golden.
Flip the rounds and brown for another 3–4 minutes on the other side, until golden and tender when pierced with a fork.
Reduce the heat to low, add the garlic and oregano and stir for 30–40 seconds, until fragrant, without letting the garlic darken.
Add the salt and serve immediately, in 4 portions, as a warm side dish.

86.b: Peas provide plant protein, fibre and vitamin K.
86.a: No major allergens in the base ingredients; check the labels of the products you use.
s: Prepare the ingredients: peel 80 g of onion and chop it finely, and peel 150 g of carrot and cut it into 0.5 cm dice. Measure out 400 g of peas (if frozen, there is no need to thaw them), 20 ml of oil, a handful of fresh dill (10 g), which you wash and chop finely, and 100 ml of water. Take out a 2–3 litre saucepan with a lid.
Heat the 20 ml of oil in the saucepan over medium heat for 1 minute. Add the onion and sauté for 3–4 minutes, stirring, until translucent.
Add the carrot and sauté for another 3–4 minutes, stirring, until slightly softened.
Add the peas, the 100 ml of water and half a teaspoon of salt (3 g). Stir and cover with the lid. Tip: if you are using frozen peas, add only 50 ml of water.
Simmer for 15 minutes over low heat, stirring once or twice, until the peas and carrot are tender when pierced with a fork and the liquid has reduced to 2–3 tablespoons.
Turn off the heat, add the chopped dill and stir. Taste and adjust the salt.
Serve hot, in 4 portions, as a side dish or a vegetarian main course.

87.b: Dark chocolate contains magnesium and polyphenols; a dessert, not a staple food.
87.a: Contains: Milk, Eggs. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Prepare the ingredients: break 150 g of dark chocolate into small pieces, separate 3 eggs (whites in a clean, dry bowl, yolks in another bowl), and measure out 30 g of sugar and 100 ml of whipping cream (cold, from the fridge). Prepare a small saucepan and a heatproof bowl that fits on top for a double boiler, 4 glasses or small bowls, and a whisk or mixer.

Put 3–4 cm of water in the saucepan and heat over low heat until the water is barely trembling, without boiling. Set the bowl with the chocolate on top, not touching the water, and melt it for 4–5 minutes, stirring, until fluid and glossy. Take the bowl off the double boiler and let it cool slightly for 5 minutes.
Whisk the egg yolks with the sugar for 2–3 minutes with the whisk or mixer, until paler and creamy. Add the cooled chocolate and stir until the mixture is smooth.

Whip the cream in a cold bowl at medium speed for 2–3 minutes, until it forms soft peaks. Fold it into the chocolate with broad, sweeping motions from the bottom up. Tip: the cream must be very cold to whip well.

Wash the whisk or mixer beaters thoroughly, then whip the egg whites for 3–4 minutes, until they form a firm foam that holds on the whisk. Fold them into the chocolate mixture in 2–3 batches, mixing gently so they do not lose their air.
Divide the mousse among 4 glasses, cover them with cling film and chill in the fridge for at least 3 hours, until set.
Serve the mousse cold, in 4 portions, straight from the glasses.

88.b: Apples provide fibre and vitamin C; eggs provide protein.
88.a: Contains: Gluten, Eggs. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Prepare the ingredients: preheat the oven to 180°C with the rack in the middle position. Grease a 24 cm round cake tin with a little oil (from the 100 ml) and line it with baking paper. Peel 400 g of apples, grate them on the coarse side of a grater and lightly drain off the excess juice. Measure out 200 g of flour, 150 g of sugar, 100 ml of oil, 8 g of baking powder and 5 g of cinnamon.
Beat the 3 eggs with the 150 g of sugar in a large bowl for 3–4 minutes with a mixer, until the mixture is paler and doubled in volume.
Add the 100 ml of oil in a thin stream, mixing continuously, until the batter is smooth.

Sift the flour with the baking powder into another bowl, then add them to the egg mixture in 2–3 batches, folding gently with a spatula. Tip: mix only until the traces of flour disappear, so the cake stays fluffy.
Add the grated apples and cinnamon and mix for another 30 seconds, until evenly distributed.
Pour the batter into the prepared tin and smooth the surface with the spatula.
Bake for 35–40 minutes at 180°C, until the cake is golden and a toothpick inserted in the centre comes out clean. Leave it in the tin for 10 minutes, then turn it out onto a wire rack.
Let the cake cool completely, cut it into 8 equal slices and serve.

89.b: Fibre from the apples; an energy-rich dessert.
89.a: Contains: Gluten, Milk, Eggs. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Prepare the ingredients: take 150 g of cold butter out of the fridge and cut it into 1 cm cubes. Measure out 300 g of flour, 1 egg, 80 g of sugar (20 g of it for the dough) and 5 g of cinnamon. Peel 600 g of apples, remove the cores and cut them into thin 0.5 cm slices. Grease a 24 cm round pie dish.

Put the flour and cold butter in a large bowl. Rub together with your fingertips for 2–3 minutes, until the texture resembles breadcrumbs. Add the egg and the 20 g of sugar and knead briefly, until it comes together into a smooth dough. Tip: do not overwork the dough, so it stays tender.
Divide the dough into 2 parts, one about 60% and the other 40%, cover them with cling film and chill in the fridge for 30 minutes, until firm.
Preheat the oven to 190°C with the rack in the middle position. Mix the apples with the remaining 60 g of sugar and the cinnamon in a bowl.
Roll out the larger piece of dough on a floured surface into a sheet 3 mm thick, and lay it in the dish, pressing it onto the bottom and sides. Fill with the apples.
Roll out the smaller piece of dough and cover the pie, then seal the edges by pressing with a fork. Prick the top 4–5 times so the steam can escape.
Bake for 35 minutes at 190°C, until the pie is golden and the filling is bubbling at the edges. Let it cool in the dish for 15 minutes.
Cut the pie into 8 equal slices and serve warm or at room temperature.

90.b: Calcium from the dairy and vitamin C from the fruit.
90.a: Contains: Milk. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Prepare the ingredients: measure out 400 ml of whipping cream, 100 ml of milk, 60 g of sugar, 8 g of gelatine (about 4 sheets or a level tablespoon of powder) and 5 ml of vanilla extract. Prepare 4 moulds or glasses of 150–200 ml, a 1.5-litre saucepan, a bowl of cold water and 150 g of washed berries.
Put the gelatine in a small bowl and cover it with 3–4 tablespoons of cold water (or just cold water for the sheets). Leave it for 5–10 minutes, until soft and gel-like.

Put the cream, milk and sugar in the saucepan and heat over low-medium heat for 4–5 minutes, stirring, until the sugar dissolves and steam rises, without letting it boil. Tip: if the mixture boils, the gelatine loses its setting power.
Take the pan off the heat and add the vanilla. Add the soaked gelatine (squeezed out if using sheets) and stir for 1–2 minutes, until completely dissolved and no granules are visible.
Let the mixture cool for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, then pour it into the 4 moulds.
Cover the moulds with cling film and chill in the fridge for at least 4 hours, until the panna cotta is set and wobbles slightly when you shake the mould.
Serve the panna cotta cold, in 4 portions, topped with the berries.

91.b: Calcium and protein from the milk.
91.a: Contains: Milk. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Prepare the ingredients: measure out 150 g of rice, 750 ml of milk, 50 g of sugar, 5 g of cinnamon and 5 ml of vanilla extract. Rinse the rice in a sieve under cold running water for 1 minute. Take out a heavy-bottomed 2–3 litre saucepan and a wooden spoon.
Put the rice and milk in the saucepan and bring to a simmer over medium heat, stirring, until small bubbles appear around the edges. Do not let the milk boil over.
Reduce the heat to low and cook for 25–30 minutes, stirring often with the wooden spoon, especially along the bottom, so it does not stick. Tip: use a heavy-bottomed pan so the milk does not scorch.
The rice is ready when the grains are soft and plump and the milk has thickened and become creamy, like a pudding.
Add the sugar and vanilla and stir for 2 minutes, until the sugar dissolves. Take the pan off the heat.
Let the rice pudding rest for 5 minutes, as it thickens as it cools.
Serve the rice pudding warm or cold, in 4 bowls, with the cinnamon sprinkled on top.

92.a: No major allergens in the base ingredients; check the labels of the products you use.
s: Prepare the ingredients: wash all the fruit well. Peel 150 g of oranges and cut them into 2 cm pieces, halve or quarter 100 g of grapes, peel 100 g of kiwi and cut it into 1.5 cm cubes, cut 150 g of apples into 1.5 cm cubes (you can leave the skin on), and peel 100 g of bananas, which you slice into 1 cm rounds. Measure out 15 ml of lemon juice and, if you like, 10 g of honey. Prepare a large bowl.
Put the chopped apples in the bowl and immediately sprinkle them with the 15 ml of lemon juice, tossing so they do not brown.
Add the oranges, grapes and kiwi to the bowl and toss gently with a large spoon so you do not crush the fruit. Tip: keep the juice that runs off the oranges, because it adds flavour.
Add the bananas last and toss just once, gently, since they soften and mash easily.
If you like, sweeten with the 10 g of honey, stirring lightly until it dissolves in the fruit juices.
Cover the bowl with cling film and chill in the fridge for 10–15 minutes so the flavours combine.
Serve the fruit salad cold, in 4 bowls or glasses, right away.

93.b: Fibre, antioxidants and healthy fats from the walnuts.
93.a: Contains: Tree nuts. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Prepare the ingredients: preheat the oven to 180°C with the rack in the middle position. Wash 4 apples (600 g in total). Chop 40 g of walnuts into 0.5 cm pieces. Measure out 20 g of honey, 5 g of cinnamon and 20 g of raisins. Prepare a small tray or a heatproof dish of about 20 x 20 cm.

Core each apple with an apple corer or a small knife, removing the core and seeds but leaving the bottom intact (about 1 cm) so the filling does not leak out. With a knife, score a shallow cut around the middle of each apple so it does not burst in the oven.
In a bowl, mix the chopped walnuts, raisins, honey and cinnamon until they form a sticky filling.
Stand the apples upright in the tray and fill each one with the filling, pressing it in lightly. Tip: if you have extra filling, pile it on top of the apples.
Pour 3–4 tablespoons of water into the tray so the bottoms of the apples do not burn.
Bake for 25–30 minutes at 180°C, until the apples are tender when pierced with a knife and the skin wrinkles slightly.
Let the apples cool slightly for 5 minutes. Serve them warm, one per portion, drizzled with the juices from the tray.

94.a: Contains: Gluten, Milk, Eggs. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Prepare the ingredients: take the butter (125 g) out of the fridge 30 minutes ahead so it softens to room temperature. Measure out 250 g of flour, 80 g of powdered sugar, 1 egg and 5 ml of vanilla extract. Preheat the oven to 170°C with the rack in the middle position, and line 2 trays with baking paper.
Put the soft butter and powdered sugar in a bowl and beat for 2–3 minutes, until the mixture is creamy and paler.
Add the egg and vanilla and mix for 1 minute, until the mixture is smooth.

Add the flour in 2–3 batches and stir with a spoon, then knead with your hands for 1–2 minutes, until you have a soft dough that does not stick. Tip: if the dough is sticky, chill it in the fridge for 15 minutes.
Roll out the dough on a floured surface into a sheet 5 mm thick and cut out shapes with a 5–6 cm cookie cutter. You will get about 20 cookies.
Place the cookies on the prepared trays, 2 cm apart.
Bake for 12–15 minutes at 170°C, until the edges turn lightly golden. Take out the trays and leave the cookies on the tray for 5 minutes, then transfer them to a wire rack.
Let the cookies cool completely, then serve. They keep in an airtight tin for 5–7 days.

95.b: Chia provides fibre, omega-3 and calcium.
95.a: Contains: Milk. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Prepare the ingredients: measure out 40 g of chia seeds, 250 ml of milk and 10 g of honey. Wash 100 g of berries. Take out a jar or bowl with a lid of about 500 ml, and a spoon.
Put the milk and honey in the jar and stir for 30 seconds, until the honey dissolves completely.
Add the chia seeds and stir for 1 minute, until evenly distributed.
Leave the mixture for 5 minutes, then stir again so the chia does not clump at the bottom. Tip: this second stir ensures an even texture.
Cover the jar with the lid and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight, until the pudding becomes thick and gel-like.
If the pudding is too thick after chilling, add 1–2 tablespoons of milk and stir.
Divide the pudding between 2 bowls and serve cold, topped with the berries.

96.b: Potassium and vitamin B6; no added sugar.
96.a: Contains: Milk. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Prepare the ingredients: peel the 3 bananas (360 g) and cut them into 1–2 cm rounds. Arrange them in a single layer on a tray lined with baking paper and freeze for 4 hours, until rock hard. Measure out 50 ml of milk and 5 g of cocoa (optional). Prepare a blender or food processor.
Take the bananas out of the freezer and leave them at room temperature for 2–3 minutes, so they do not damage the blender blade.

Put the bananas in the blender and add the 50 ml of milk. Blend on low speed for 30 seconds, then stop and scrape down the sides with a spatula. Tip: if the blender gets stuck, add 1–2 tablespoons of milk.
Blend on high speed for another 1–2 minutes, until you get a creamy, soft-serve texture with no lumps.
If you like, add the 5 g of cocoa and blend for 20 seconds, until evenly distributed.
Serve immediately in 2 bowls for a soft texture. For a firmer consistency, put it in the freezer for 30 minutes.

97.b: Calcium and protein from the milk.
97.a: Contains: Gluten, Milk. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Prepare the ingredients: measure out 40 g of semolina, 400 ml of milk, 20 g of sugar and 5 g of cinnamon. Take out a heavy-bottomed 1-litre saucepan and a whisk or wooden spoon. Prepare 2 serving bowls.

Put the milk and sugar in the saucepan and heat over medium heat for 3–4 minutes, stirring occasionally, until small bubbles appear around the edges and the milk begins to simmer. Do not let it boil over.
Reduce the heat to low and add the semolina in a steady rain, a little at a time, stirring continuously with the whisk so no lumps form. Tip: pour the semolina with one hand and stir with the other.
Cook for 4–5 minutes, stirring constantly, until the mixture thickens and becomes creamy, like a slightly runny pudding.
Take the saucepan off the heat and let the semolina rest for 1–2 minutes, as it thickens a little as it cools.
Divide the semolina between 2 bowls and serve warm, with the cinnamon sprinkled on top.

98.b: Fibre from the oats; a more filling dessert.
98.a: Contains: Gluten, Milk, Eggs. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Prepare the ingredients: preheat the oven to 180°C with the rack in the middle position and line 2 trays with baking paper. Melt 80 g of butter in a small saucepan over low heat for 2 minutes, then let it cool slightly for 5 minutes. Measure out 150 g of rolled oats, 100 g of flour, 80 g of brown sugar, 1 egg, 50 g of raisins and 5 g of baking powder.
Mix the melted butter with the brown sugar in a large bowl for 1 minute, until combined. Add the egg and whisk for 1 minute, until the mixture is smooth and glossy.
Add the oats, flour and baking powder to the mixture and combine with a spoon until no dry patches remain.
Add the raisins and mix for another 30 seconds, until evenly distributed. Tip: if the dough is too dry, add 1 tablespoon of milk or water.
With damp hands, shape 12 balls of about 40 g each, place them on the trays 4–5 cm apart and flatten them lightly until they are 1 cm thick.
Bake for 12–15 minutes at 180°C, until the edges are golden and the centre is still slightly soft (it firms up as it cools).
Take out the trays and leave the cookies on the tray for 5 minutes, then transfer them to a wire rack. Serve once completely cooled.

99.a: Contains: Gluten, Eggs. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Prepare the ingredients: preheat the oven to 175°C with the rack in the middle position. Line the bottom of a 24 cm round tin with baking paper and leave the sides ungreased. Separate 4 eggs, and measure out 120 g of sugar, 120 g of flour and 5 ml of vanilla extract. You will need a mixer and a large, clean, dry bowl.

Put the yolks, the whites (together) and the sugar in the bowl and beat with the mixer on high speed for 8–10 minutes, until the mixture becomes a thick, pale foam that falls in a ribbon and holds its shape for 3–4 seconds.
Add the vanilla and beat for another 20 seconds. Tip: the bowl and beaters must be perfectly clean, with no trace of grease, otherwise the eggs will not whip properly.
Sift the flour over the foam in 3 batches and fold it in with a spatula, using broad motions from the bottom up, gently, so you do not lose the air.
Pour the batter into the prepared tin and tap it lightly on the counter once to release the large air bubbles.
Bake for 25–30 minutes at 175°C, until the sponge is golden and a toothpick inserted in the centre comes out clean. Do not open the oven during the first 20 minutes.
Take out the tin, leave the sponge for 5 minutes, then loosen the edges with a knife and turn it out onto a wire rack. Let it cool completely.
Cut the sponge into 8 equal slices and serve plain or with fruit.

100.b: Vitamin A from the pumpkin, good for immunity.
100.a: Contains: Milk. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Prepare the ingredients: peel 600 g of pumpkin and remove the seeds, then cut it into 2–3 cm cubes, peel 150 g of potatoes and cut them into 2 cm cubes, and peel 100 g of onion and chop it finely. Measure out 700 ml of water, 20 ml of oil, 100 ml of cooking cream, 15 g of pumpkin seeds (optional) and some salt. Take out a 3–4 litre pot and a hand blender.
Heat the 20 ml of oil in the pot over medium heat for 1 minute. Add the onion and sauté for 4–5 minutes, stirring, until soft and translucent.
Add the pumpkin and potatoes to the pot and stir for 2–3 minutes, so they are coated in oil and onion.
Pour in the 700 ml of water, add a teaspoon of salt (5 g) and bring to a boil over high heat. Then reduce the heat to low.
Simmer for 25 minutes, partially covered, until the pumpkin and potatoes are completely soft when pierced with a fork. Tip: if the liquid reduces too much, add 100 ml of hot water.
Take the pot off the heat and blend the soup with the hand blender for 2–3 minutes, until smooth and free of lumps.
Add the cooking cream, stir and warm for 1–2 minutes over low heat, without boiling. Taste and adjust the salt.
Serve the soup hot, in 4 bowls, with the pumpkin seeds sprinkled on top.

101.b: Vitamins C and K, and folate.
101.a: Contains: Milk, Celery. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Prepare the ingredients: wash 500 g of broccoli and break it into small florets, also cutting the stalk into 1 cm pieces, peel 150 g of potatoes and cut them into 2 cm cubes, and peel 100 g of onion and chop it finely. Measure out 700 ml of stock (vegetable or meat), 100 ml of cooking cream, 15 g of butter and some salt. Take out a 3-litre pot and a hand blender.
Melt the 15 g of butter in the pot over medium heat for 1 minute. Add the onion and sauté for 3–4 minutes, stirring, until translucent, without browning.
Add the potatoes and broccoli to the pot and stir for 1–2 minutes.
Pour in the 700 ml of stock, bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to low.
Simmer for 15–20 minutes, partially covered, until the broccoli and potatoes are completely soft when pierced with a fork. Tip: do not overcook the broccoli, so the soup keeps its green colour.
Take the pot off the heat and blend the soup with the hand blender for 2–3 minutes, until smooth and creamy.
Add the cooking cream, stir and warm for 1–2 minutes over low heat. Taste and adjust the salt.
Serve the cream soup hot, in 4 bowls.

102.b: Lentils provide iron, folate, fibre and plant protein.
102.a: No major allergens in the base ingredients; check the labels of the products you use.
s: Prepare the ingredients: rinse 200 g of lentils in a sieve under cold running water for 1 minute and pick out any impurities. Peel 100 g of carrot and cut it into 0.5 cm dice, peel 100 g of onion and chop it finely, and peel 2 garlic cloves and mince them. Measure out 5 g of cumin, 1 litre of water, 15 ml of oil and 15 ml of lemon juice. Take out a 3-litre pot.
Heat the 15 ml of oil in the pot over medium heat for 1 minute. Add the onion and carrot and sauté for 4–5 minutes, stirring, until the onion is translucent and the carrot is slightly softened.
Add the garlic and sauté for 30 seconds, stirring, until fragrant. Tip: do not let the garlic brown, so the soup does not taste bitter.
Add the lentils, cumin and the 1000 ml of water and stir. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to low.
Simmer for 25–30 minutes, partially covered, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are soft and easily crushed between your fingers. If foam forms on the surface, skim it off with a spoon.
Add a teaspoon of salt (5 g) about 20 minutes into cooking, so the lentils soften evenly. If you would like a thicker soup, blend about half of it with a hand blender.
Take the pot off the heat and add the 15 ml of lemon juice. Taste and adjust the salt.
Serve the soup hot, in 4 bowls.

35.b: Carbohydrates for energy and unsaturated fats from the olive oil.
s: Prepare the ingredients: measure out 400 g of flour, 300 ml of room-temperature water (neither cold nor hot), 7 g of dry yeast, 5 g of salt, 30 ml of olive oil and 5 g of rosemary. Get out a large bowl, a wooden spoon, a clean kitchen towel and a baking tin of about 25 x 35 cm greased with a little oil.
Put the flour, dry yeast and salt in the bowl and mix them briefly with the spoon. Tip: at first, keep the salt and yeast on opposite sides of the bowl so they don't touch directly.
Pour the 300 ml of water over the flour and mix for 1–2 minutes, until there are no dry patches of flour left. The dough will be sticky and soft, which is normal for focaccia.
With wet hands, knead the dough in the bowl for 3–4 minutes, stretching it and folding it over itself, until it becomes smoother and more elastic.

Cover the bowl with the clean towel and leave the dough to rise in a warm place, away from drafts, for 1 hour to 1 hour 30 minutes, until it has doubled in volume and bubbles are visible on the surface.

Turn the dough out into the greased tin and spread it with your fingers almost to the edges. If it springs back, let it rest for 5 minutes and stretch it again. Tip: grease your fingers with oil so the dough doesn't stick.
Cover the tin and let the dough rise for another 20–30 minutes. Meanwhile, heat the oven to 220°C, with the rack in the middle position.

Brush the surface with the 30 ml of olive oil. Press your fingertips into the dough to make dimples all over the surface, almost down to the bottom of the tin, then sprinkle with the rosemary and a little extra salt if you like.
Bake the focaccia for 20–25 minutes, until golden and crisp at the edges. If it browns too quickly on top, cover it with a sheet of baking paper.

Take the tin out of the oven and let the focaccia rest for 5 minutes, then move it to a wire rack or a board. Cut it into squares and serve warm, as a side or a snack. It keeps wrapped in foil at room temperature for 1–2 days.

36.b: Provides carbohydrates; wholemeal flour increases the intake of fibre and minerals.
s: Measure out 500 g of flour, 330 ml of lukewarm water (about 30–35°C, like a baby's bath water), 7 g of dry yeast and 10 g of salt. Get ready a large bowl, a wooden spoon, a clean towel and a baking tin lined with baking paper (or a 25 cm loaf tin).

Pour the lukewarm water into the bowl, add the yeast and stir. Leave for 5 minutes, until small bubbles appear on the surface. Tip: water that is too hot kills the yeast, so check it with your finger.
Add the flour and salt, plus the oil if you are using the oil version (10 ml). Mix with the spoon until a shaggy dough forms, with no dry flour left.

Turn the dough out onto the floured work surface and knead it for 8–10 minutes, pressing it with the heel of your hand and folding it over. It is ready when it is smooth, elastic and springs back slowly when you press it with a finger.
Put the dough back into the lightly greased bowl, cover it with the towel and leave it to rise in a warm place for 1 hour to 1 hour 30 minutes, until doubled in volume.
Knock the air out of the dough by gently pressing it with your fist. Shape it into a ball or an elongated loaf, tucking the edges underneath, and place it in the tin seam side down.

Cover the shaped dough and let it rise for another 20–30 minutes, until it looks visibly puffed up. Meanwhile, heat the oven to 220°C and, if you like, put a dish with a little water on the bottom rack to create steam. Tip: slash the loaf with a very sharp knife just before baking so it rises nicely.
Bake the bread for 30–35 minutes, until it has a dark golden crust. Tap the base lightly: if it sounds hollow, it is done.

Remove the bread from the tin and leave it on a wire rack for at least 30 minutes before slicing, so the crumb can set. Serve in slices with any meal. It keeps wrapped in a towel at room temperature for 2–3 days.

37.b: The cheese and yogurt provide protein and calcium; the eggs add protein and choline.
s: Take the pastry sheets out of the fridge 30 minutes ahead so they don't tear. Melt the 50 g of butter over low heat or in the microwave. Get ready a baking tin of about 25 x 35 cm, a large bowl, a pastry brush or a spoon for greasing, and a knife.
Heat the oven to 180°C. Grease the tin with a little of the melted butter.

In the bowl, mix the 400 g of cottage cheese, the 2 eggs, the 150 g of yogurt and, if you like, 10 g of sugar. Stir until the mixture is smooth. Tip: mash any lumps of cheese with a fork so the filling is creamy.
Lay the first pastry sheet in the tin, letting the edges hang over slightly. Brush it with melted butter. Repeat with 3–4 more sheets, brushing each one.
Spread half of the cheese filling over the sheets in the tin in an even layer. Cover with 2 more sheets brushed with butter.
Add the rest of the filling, smooth it out and cover with the remaining sheets, brushing each with butter. Fold the overhanging edges over the pie and brush the remaining butter on top.
Before baking, cut the pie into squares, slicing only through the top sheets, so it cuts easily after baking.
Bake the pie at 180°C for 35–40 minutes, until evenly browned and the filling is firm to the touch. Tip: if it browns too quickly, cover the tin with aluminium foil.
Let the pie rest in the tin for 10 minutes, then serve warm or at room temperature. It keeps in the fridge, covered, for 2–3 days.

38.b: Bananas provide potassium and vitamin B6; milk provides protein and calcium.
38.a: Milk; honey is not suitable for vegans.
s: Peel the 2 bananas and slice them into rounds about 1–2 cm thick. Measure 300 ml of (cold) milk and take out 4–5 ice cubes. Get the blender and 2 glasses ready.
Put the bananas, milk and ice cubes in the blender. Tip: for an even creamier smoothie, use frozen bananas instead of ice.
Add 10 g of honey if you want it sweeter. For a vegan version, use a plant-based drink instead of milk and leave out the honey; for a lactose-free version, use lactose-free milk.
Blend for 30–60 seconds, until the drink is smooth with no pieces of ice. Taste and add a little more honey if needed.
Pour the smoothie into glasses and serve immediately, so it doesn't darken.

39.b: The fruit provides fibre, vitamin C and antioxidants; the yogurt adds protein and calcium.
39.a: Milk (from the yogurt); check any added ingredients.
s: Wash 150 g of strawberries and 100 g of blueberries under cold running water and drain them. Remove the strawberry hulls and cut the berries in half. Peel the banana and slice it into rounds. Measure 200 g of yogurt and 50 ml of water.
Put the yogurt, water, banana, strawberries and blueberries in the blender. Tip: add the liquids first, then the fruit, so the blades spin more easily.
Blend for 40–60 seconds, until the smoothie is creamy and free of lumps. If it is too thick, add water a spoonful at a time and blend again.
For a vegan version, use plant-based yogurt. Pour into glasses and serve immediately, or keep for up to 24 hours in the fridge in a closed bottle; shake before drinking.

40.b: Oranges provide vitamin C; carrots contain beta-carotene. The juice has less fibre than whole fruit.
40.a: Usually none of the 14 major allergens; check any additional ingredients.
s: Wash the 3 oranges and 2 carrots well. Peel the carrots and trim off the ends. Cut the oranges in half. Get ready a citrus juicer, a blender, a sieve and a glass or bowl.
Squeeze the oranges with the citrus juicer or by hand until you have extracted all the juice. Tip: roll the oranges on the counter before cutting them so they give more juice.

Cut the carrots into 1 cm rounds and put them in the blender with 100 ml of water (if needed). Blend for 1–2 minutes, until you get a fine purée. If you have an electric juicer, you can juice the carrots directly, without water.
Strain the carrot purée through a fine sieve, pressing with a spoon to separate the pulp from the juice. Mix the carrot juice with the orange juice.
Serve the juice immediately, with or without ice. It keeps in the fridge in a closed bottle for up to 24 hours.

41.b: Milk and ice cream provide calcium and protein; the fruit adds vitamins.
41.a: Milk; the ice cream may contain eggs, soy or nuts.
s: Wash the strawberries (or peel the banana) and cut them into small pieces, about 2 cm. Take the ice cream out of the freezer 5 minutes ahead so it softens slightly. Measure 300 ml of cold milk, 200 g of vanilla ice cream and 150 g of fruit.
Put the milk in the blender, then the ice cream and the fruit pieces. Tip: very cold milk makes a thicker, frothier milkshake.
Blend for 30–45 seconds, until the drink is creamy with no ice crystals. If it is too thick, add a little more milk.
Pour the milkshake into 2 tall glasses and serve immediately, with straws. Check the ice cream label for allergens.

42.b: Spinach provides folate and vitamin K; the apple and banana add fibre and potassium.
42.a: The basic recipe contains none of the major allergens; check any additions.
s: Wash the 60 g of spinach well and drain it. Wash the apple, remove the core and cut it into 2 cm cubes (you can leave the skin on). Peel the banana and slice it into rounds. Measure 250 ml of water and 10 ml of lemon juice.
Put the water, lemon juice, spinach, apple and banana in the blender. Tip: put the spinach on top of the liquid so it blends better.
Blend for 1 minute on high speed, until no whole leaves remain and the drink is smooth. Taste and, if it is too sour, add a little extra banana.
Pour the smoothie into 2 glasses and serve immediately. It can be kept in the fridge in a closed bottle for 24 hours; shake before drinking.

43.b: Meat provides protein, iron and vitamin B12.
43.a: Contains: Gluten, Eggs. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Prepare the ingredients: soak 100 g of bread in water for 5 minutes, then squeeze it out well with your hands. Peel 80 g of onion and grate it on the fine side of the grater. Crush the 2 garlic cloves. Finely chop the parsley. Get out a large bowl, a plate with 40 g of breadcrumbs and a large frying pan.
In a bowl, put the 500 g of minced meat, the squeezed bread broken into small pieces, the egg, the grated onion, the garlic and the parsley. Add salt and pepper to taste.
Knead the mixture with your hands for 3–4 minutes, until it is smooth and pulls away from the sides of the bowl. Tip: if the mixture sticks to your hands, dampen them with cold water.
Leave the mixture in the fridge for 10 minutes so it firms up a little and is easier to shape. If you like, fry a tiny piece of the mixture and taste it to check the seasoning.
With wet hands, shape the mixture into meatballs the size of a large ping-pong ball (about 60–70 g each) and flatten them slightly. Roll them in the breadcrumbs, shaking off the excess.
Heat the 40 ml of oil in the frying pan over medium heat, until a breadcrumb sizzles as soon as it hits the oil.

Add the meatballs to the pan without crowding them and fry for 12–15 minutes in total, turning them every 3 minutes, until evenly browned and no longer pink inside (75°C in the centre). Tip: fry them in two batches so the oil doesn't cool down.
Transfer the meatballs to a plate lined with kitchen paper to drain off the oil. Serve warm, with mashed potatoes or a salad. They keep in the fridge in a closed container for 3 days.

44.b: Chicken provides protein and niacin; the vegetables add vitamin C.
44.a: No major allergens in the basic ingredients; check the labels of the products you use.
s: Wash the 700 g of chicken legs and pat them dry with kitchen paper. Peel 150 g of onion and chop it finely. Crush the 2 garlic cloves. Cut 150 g of peppers into 1–2 cm cubes and the 200 g of tomatoes into 2 cm cubes. Measure 10 g of sweet paprika, 300 ml of water and 30 ml of oil. Get out a heavy-bottomed pot or saucepan of 3–4 litres.
Season the chicken legs with salt on all sides. Heat the oil in the pot over medium-high heat for 1 minute.

Put the chicken legs in the pot, skin side down, and brown them for 4–5 minutes on each side, until golden. Transfer them to a plate. Tip: don't crowd the pieces, otherwise they steam instead of browning.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add the onion to the same pot and sauté for 4–5 minutes, stirring, until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic and peppers and sauté for 2–3 minutes, stirring. Take the pot off the heat for 30 seconds, add the sweet paprika and stir well so it doesn't burn (burnt paprika makes the dish bitter).
Put the pot back on the heat, add the tomatoes and cook for 3–4 minutes, until they start to break down and form a sauce.
Return the chicken legs to the pot and pour in the 300 ml of water. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and cover the pot.
Simmer over low heat for 35–40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the meat pulls easily away from the bone, there is no pink left and the sauce has thickened. Taste and adjust the salt.
Serve the stew hot, with polenta (mămăligă), rice or boiled potatoes. It keeps in the fridge in a closed container for 3 days; reheat it over low heat.

45.b: Beef is rich in iron, zinc and vitamin B12.
45.a: No major allergens in the basic ingredients; check the labels of the products you use.
s: Wash the 800 g of beef and pat it dry with paper towels, then cut it into 2–3 cm cubes. Finely chop 200 g of onion, cut 150 g of peppers into 2 cm cubes and cut 300 g of peeled potatoes into 2–3 cm cubes (keep them in cold water until you use them). Crush the 2 garlic cloves. Measure 15 g of sweet paprika, 30 g of tomato paste and 1 litre of water, and take out a bay leaf. Get out a pot of 4–5 litres.

Heat the 30 ml of oil in the pot over high heat. Add the meat in two batches and brown it for 5–6 minutes, until it has a golden crust on all sides. Season with salt after browning. Tip: don't stir too often, so a crust can form.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add the onion on top of the meat and cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until soft and lightly golden.
Add the garlic, tomato paste and sweet paprika. Stir for 1 minute so the paste caramelises slightly. Take the pot off the heat before adding the paprika so it doesn't burn.
Pour in the 1000 ml of water, add the bay leaf and salt, and bring to a boil. Skim off the foam that forms on the surface with a spoon.
Reduce the heat to low, cover the pot with the lid slightly ajar and simmer for 80 minutes, stirring occasionally. Add a little hot water if it reduces too much.

Add the drained potatoes and the peppers. Simmer for another 25–30 minutes, until the potatoes are tender when pierced with a fork and the meat falls apart easily. Tip: the goulash should keep a thickened sauce, not too thin.
Remove the bay leaf, taste and adjust the salt. Let the goulash rest for 10 minutes, then serve hot with fresh bread. It keeps in the fridge for 3–4 days and can be frozen.

46.b: A complete dish: protein from the chicken and carbohydrates from the potatoes.
46.a: No major allergens in the basic ingredients; check the labels of the products you use.
s: Heat the oven to 200°C. Wash the potatoes (800 g) and either peel them or leave the skin on, then cut them into thick slices of 1.5–2 cm. Crush the 4 garlic cloves. Wash the chicken legs (800 g) and pat them dry with kitchen paper. Get out a large baking tray and a bowl.
Put the potatoes in the bowl with half of the 30 ml of oil, salt, pepper and rosemary and toss well so they are evenly coated.
Put the chicken legs in another bowl and rub them on all sides with the rest of the oil, the 10 g of smoked paprika, the crushed garlic, salt and pepper.
Spread the potatoes in the tray in a single layer. Place the chicken legs on top, skin side up. Tip: put the legs skin side up so the skin browns and turns crisp.
Put the tray in the heated oven and bake for 50 minutes in total. After 25 minutes, take out the tray and stir the potatoes, then turn the chicken legs over.
Check that the chicken is cooked: the juices should run clear, with no pink, and the meat should reach 75°C at the thickest part. The potatoes should be golden and tender.
If the skin is not browned enough, return the tray to the oven for 5 more minutes. Take out the tray and let it rest for 5 minutes.
Serve the chicken legs hot, with the potatoes, alongside a fresh salad. They keep in the fridge in a closed container for 2–3 days.

47.b: Salmon provides protein, omega-3 fatty acids and vitamin D.
47.a: Contains: Fish. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Take the salmon out of the fridge 10 minutes ahead. Heat the oven to 200°C. Cut the lemon into thin slices of 3–4 mm (remove the seeds). Crush the 2 garlic cloves and finely chop the dill. Line a small baking tray with baking paper.
Pat the 300 g of salmon dry with kitchen paper. Place it in the tray, skin side down.
Mix the 15 ml of olive oil with the crushed garlic, salt and pepper. Brush the mixture over the whole surface of the salmon.
Cover the salmon with the lemon slices and sprinkle with the dill. Tip: put lemon both under and on top of the fish for a better flavour.
Bake the salmon for 12–15 minutes, depending on thickness, until the flesh turns opaque and flakes easily into layers with a fork (the fish reaches 63°C inside).
Take out the tray and let the salmon rest for 2 minutes. Serve with lemon slices, alongside boiled potatoes or a salad. It keeps in the fridge in a closed container for 1–2 days.

48.b: Fish provides easily digestible protein, vitamin D and omega-3.
48.a: Contains: Gluten, Milk, Fish. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Check that the trout (2, 400 g) are properly cleaned and rinse them in cold water, then pat them very dry with kitchen paper, inside as well. Finely chop the parsley. Measure 30 g of flour onto a plate, 30 ml of oil, 20 g of butter and 15 ml of lemon juice. Get out a large frying pan, a wide spatula and a plate.
Season the fish with salt on both sides and inside. Leave them for 5 minutes, then pat off any excess moisture again.
Dredge each fish in the flour, on both sides, and shake off the excess flour. Tip: use only a thin coating of flour, otherwise the crust turns pasty.
Heat the oil in the pan over medium-high heat, until a pinch of flour sizzles immediately.
Put the trout in the pan and cook for 5–6 minutes on the first side, without moving them, until a golden crust forms. Carefully turn them with the spatula.
Cook for another 5–6 minutes on the other side, until the flesh flakes easily at the thickest part and is no longer translucent.
Reduce the heat to low, add the butter and let it melt, then pour in the lemon juice and sprinkle with the parsley. Spoon the sauce from the pan over the fish.
Serve immediately, with boiled potatoes or green salad. Fish is best eaten fresh; leftovers keep in the fridge for 1 day.

49.b: Shrimp are a lean source of protein and selenium.
49.a: Contains: Milk, Crustaceans. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: If the shrimp are frozen, thaw them in cold water for 10–15 minutes, then drain them and pat them dry with kitchen paper (300 g). Peel the 4 garlic cloves and cut them into thin slices. Chop the parsley. Measure 30 ml of olive oil, 20 g of butter, 15 ml of lemon juice and a small teaspoon (as much as you like) of chilli flakes. Get out a large frying pan.
Lightly season the shrimp with salt. Heat the oil with the butter in the pan over low-medium heat until the butter melts.
Add the garlic and cook for 30–60 seconds, stirring, until fragrant but not browned. Tip: burnt garlic is bitter, so take the pan off the heat if it browns quickly.
Increase the heat to medium-high. Add the shrimp to the pan in a single layer and cook for 2–3 minutes on the first side, until they turn pink.
Turn the shrimp and cook for another 2–3 minutes, until pink and opaque and curled into a C shape. Don't overcook them, or they become rubbery.
Take the pan off the heat, add the lemon juice, chilli flakes and parsley and stir.
Serve immediately, with fresh bread for mopping up the sauce, or with rice. They keep in the fridge for 1 day; reheat briefly over low heat.

50.b: Pork provides protein and vitamin B1.
50.a: Contains: Mustard. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Take the chops (2, 400 g) out of the fridge 15–20 minutes ahead and pat them dry with paper. Crush the 2 garlic cloves and get the thyme ready. Measure 10 g of mustard and 20 ml of oil. Get out a large frying pan with a lid and a plate.
Mix the mustard with the crushed garlic, thyme, salt and pepper in a small bowl until you have a paste.
Spread the mustard paste on both sides of the chops. Leave them for 10 minutes to take on the flavours. Tip: if you have time, marinate them for 30 minutes.
Heat the oil in the pan over medium-high heat, until a light wisp of steam begins to show.
Put the chops in the pan and brown them for 5 minutes on the first side, without moving them, until they form a golden crust.
Turn the chops and brown them for 5 minutes on the other side as well.
Reduce the heat to low, cover the pan with the lid and cook for another 8–10 minutes, until the meat is no longer pink inside and the juices run clear (about 70°C in the centre).
Transfer the chops to the plate and let them rest for 5 minutes so they stay juicy. Serve with a salad or a side of potatoes. They keep in the fridge for 2 days.

51.b: Chicken provides protein; curry powder adds antioxidants from the spices.
51.a: No major allergens in the basic ingredients; check the labels of the products you use.
s: Wash the chicken breast (500 g), pat it dry and cut it into 2–3 cm cubes. Peel 150 g of onion and chop it finely. Crush the 2 garlic cloves and grate 10 g of ginger on the fine side of the grater. Measure 200 g of rice, 200 g of passata, 200 ml of coconut milk, 10 g of curry powder and 30 ml of oil. Get out a deep frying pan or a 3-litre saucepan and a pot for the rice.

Rinse the rice in a sieve under cold running water until the water runs clearer. Put the rice in the pot with 400 ml of water and a little salt, bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover and cook for 12–15 minutes, until the water is absorbed and the grains are tender. Leave covered for another 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Heat the oil in the deep frying pan over medium heat. Add the onion and sauté for 4–5 minutes, until translucent.
Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute, stirring, then sprinkle in the curry powder and stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant. Tip: spices release more flavour when briefly heated in oil.
Add the chicken, salted to taste, and brown it for 4–5 minutes, stirring, until it changes colour on all sides.
Pour in the passata and coconut milk. Stir and bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low.
Simmer for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens and the chicken is cooked through, with no pink at all in the middle (75°C). Taste and adjust the salt.
Serve the curry hot, over the cooked rice. It keeps in the fridge in a closed container for 3 days; reheat thoroughly before eating.

52.b: Meat and beans: protein, iron and fibre.
52.a: No major allergens in the basic ingredients; check the labels of the products you use.
s: Peel 150 g of onion and chop it finely. Crush the 2 garlic cloves. Cut 150 g of peppers into 1 cm cubes. Drain the canned beans (400 g) in a sieve and rinse them under cold running water. Measure 500 g of minced meat, 400 g of chopped tomatoes, 5 g of hot paprika, 5 g of cumin and 30 ml of oil. Get out a 3–4 litre pot.
Heat the oil in the pot over medium heat. Add the onion and sauté for 4–5 minutes, until translucent.
Add the garlic and peppers and cook for 3–4 minutes, stirring, until slightly softened.
Turn the heat up to high, add the minced meat and salt and brown it for 6–8 minutes, breaking it up with the wooden spoon, until no longer pink.
Sprinkle in the hot paprika and cumin and stir for 1 minute, until fragrant. Tip: for less heat, use half the hot paprika.
Add the chopped tomatoes and the drained beans. Stir and bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low.
Simmer over low heat for 35–40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens. If it dries out too much, add a little water.
Taste and adjust the salt. Let it rest for 5 minutes and serve warm, with rice or bread. It keeps in the fridge for 3–4 days; it is even better the next day.

53.b: Protein from the meat, calcium from the cheese, vitamins from the vegetables.
53.a: Contains: Gluten, Milk. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Peel 100 g of onion and chop it finely. Wash the tomatoes (200 g) and dice them into 1 cm cubes. Wash the lettuce (80 g), cut it into thin strips and drain it. Grate the cheddar (100 g). Measure 400 g of minced meat, 5 g of cumin and 5 g of paprika. Get out a large frying pan and a plate for the tortillas.
Put the pan over high heat, without oil, for 1 minute. Add the minced meat and brown it for 5–6 minutes, breaking it up with the wooden spoon.
Add the onion, cumin, paprika, and salt and pepper to taste. Cook over medium heat for 5 minutes, stirring, until the onion is soft and the meat has no pink left.
Taste the meat and adjust the seasoning. Take the pan off the heat. Tip: drain off any excess fat, if there is a lot, so the tacos don't turn soggy.
Warm the tortillas one at a time in a dry frying pan, 20–30 seconds on each side, until pliable.
Put a portion of meat on each tortilla, then the tomatoes, lettuce and cheddar. Don't overfill, so they can be folded closed.
Fold the tortillas and serve immediately, while the meat is warm and the lettuce is crisp. Leftover meat keeps in the fridge for 2–3 days, separate from the vegetables.

54.b: Provides protein, iron and carbohydrates for energy.
54.a: Contains: Gluten, Milk. Check the labels of the products you use.
