s: Wash the tomatoes (150 g) and cut them into 5 mm slices. Wash the lettuce (60 g) and drain it. Peel the onion (80 g) and cut it into thin slices. Get out the cheese (4 slices) and the buns (4). Get ready a large frying pan, a spatula and a plate.
Put the 500 g of minced meat in a bowl, add salt and pepper and mix gently with your hands, without squashing the meat too much. Tip: the less you knead it, the more tender the burger stays.

Divide the meat into 4 equal portions (about 125 g each) and shape 4 flat patties, 1.5–2 cm thick and slightly wider than the buns. Press the centre with your finger so they don't puff up while cooking.
Heat the pan over high heat for 2 minutes. Add the patties (in 2 batches if they don't all fit) and cook them for 4–5 minutes on the first side, without moving them, until browned.
Flip the patties and cook for another 4–5 minutes, until no pink remains in the middle (75°C). Place a slice of cheese on each and cover the pan for 1 minute so it melts.
Cut the buns in half and toast them in the pan, cut side down, for 1 minute, until lightly browned.
Assemble the burgers: spread ketchup (30 g in total) on the bottom bun, then add the lettuce, tomatoes, the patty with cheese, the onion and the top bun.
Serve immediately, with fries or a salad. Cooked patties keep in the fridge for 2 days.

55.b: Carbohydrates for energy; basil and olive oil provide vitamins K and E.
55.a: Contains: Gluten, Milk, Tree nuts. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Put 3–4 litres of water in a large pot over high heat and cover the pot. Wash the cherry tomatoes (150 g) and cut them in half. Measure 320 g of pasta, 100 g of pesto and 30 g of Parmesan; grate the Parmesan finely. Get out a colander and a bowl.
When the water boils, add 1–2 tablespoons of salt (about 15–20 g) and the pasta. Stir at the start so it doesn't stick.
Cook the pasta according to the package instructions, usually 9–11 minutes, until al dente (firm to the bite). Tip: taste a piece 1 minute before the time is up.
Before draining, scoop out about 100 ml of the cooking water with a cup and set it aside. Drain the pasta in the colander.
Return the pasta to the pot, take it off the heat, and add the pesto and 3–4 tablespoons of the cooking water. Stir well, until the sauce coats the pasta evenly. Add more water if it is too thick.
Add the halved cherry tomatoes and half of the Parmesan. Stir gently.
Serve immediately on warm plates, with the rest of the Parmesan on top. It keeps in the fridge in a closed container for 2 days.

56.b: Salmon provides omega-3, vitamin D and protein.
56.a: Contains: Gluten, Milk, Fish. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Put 3–4 litres of water on to boil in a large pot. Pat the salmon (250 g) dry with kitchen paper and cut it into 2 cm cubes, removing the skin and any small bones. Crush the 2 garlic cloves and finely chop the dill. Measure 320 g of pasta, 200 ml of cooking cream and 20 g of butter. Get out a large frying pan.
Add 1–2 tablespoons of salt and the pasta to the boiling water. Cook for 9–11 minutes, according to the package, until al dente. Scoop out 100 ml of the cooking water, then drain the pasta.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in the pan over medium heat. Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds, until fragrant. Tip: don't let the garlic brown, so it doesn't turn bitter.
Add the salmon cubes, salt and pepper and cook for 3–4 minutes, turning them gently, until they are opaque and light pink on all sides.
Pour in the 200 ml of cooking cream, reduce the heat to low and let it simmer gently for 2–3 minutes, until it thickens slightly.
Add the drained pasta to the pan and stir gently so the salmon doesn't break apart. If the sauce is too thick, add a spoonful of the cooking water at a time.
Take it off the heat, sprinkle with the dill and taste. Serve immediately. It keeps in the fridge for 1–2 days; reheat over low heat with a little water.

57.b: Mushrooms provide B vitamins and selenium; pasta provides energy.
57.a: Contains: Gluten, Milk. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Put 3–4 litres of water on to boil in a large pot. Wipe the mushrooms (300 g) with a damp cloth or rinse them quickly, and cut them into 5 mm slices. Peel the onion (100 g) and chop it finely. Crush the 2 garlic cloves. Chop the parsley. If you are using Parmesan (30 g), grate it. Measure 320 g of pasta, 200 ml of cooking cream and 20 ml of oil.
Add 1–2 tablespoons of salt and the pasta to the boiling water and cook for 9–11 minutes, until al dente. Scoop out 100 ml of the cooking water and drain the pasta.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Add the onion and sauté for 3–4 minutes, until translucent.
Turn the heat up to high, add the mushrooms and cook for 6–8 minutes, stirring only occasionally, until they release their water and brown. Tip: don't salt them at the start, so they brown better.
Add the garlic, salt and pepper and cook for 1 minute, stirring.
Pour in the cream, reduce the heat to low and simmer for 2–3 minutes, until the sauce thickens slightly.
Add the drained pasta and mix well. If the sauce is thick, add a little of the cooking water. Take it off the heat and sprinkle with the parsley and Parmesan.
Serve immediately, on warm plates. It keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

58.b: Rice provides energy; mushrooms and Parmesan add protein and minerals.
58.a: Contains: Milk, Celery. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Put the hot stock (1 l) in a small pot over very low heat so it stays hot throughout the cooking. Clean the mushrooms (300 g) with a damp cloth and cut them into 5 mm slices. Peel the onion (100 g) and chop it finely. Grate the Parmesan (50 g). Measure 300 g of rice, 100 ml of white wine and 40 g of butter. Get out a wide, heavy-bottomed saucepan and a wooden spoon.
Melt half of the butter (20 g) in the saucepan over medium heat. Add the mushrooms and cook for 6–8 minutes, until browned and their liquid has cooked off. Transfer them to a bowl.
Add the remaining butter and the onion to the saucepan. Sauté for 3–4 minutes, stirring, until translucent.
Add the rice and stir for 1–2 minutes, until the grains turn translucent at the edges. Tip: the rice should be well coated in fat so it doesn't stick.
Pour in the white wine and stir until it evaporates, about 1–2 minutes.

Add the hot stock one ladleful at a time, stirring constantly, and wait until it is almost absorbed before adding the next ladleful. Continue for 18–20 minutes, until the rice is creamy but the grains still have a slight firmness at the centre.
Return the mushrooms to the pan and stir. Take the saucepan off the heat, add the Parmesan and stir vigorously until creamy. Taste and adjust the salt and pepper.
Leave the risotto covered for 2 minutes, then serve immediately on warm plates. It keeps in the fridge for 1–2 days.

59.b: A hearty dish with protein, carbohydrates and calcium.
59.a: Contains: Gluten, Milk, Eggs. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Peel the potatoes (800 g) and cut them into 5 mm slices. Peel the onion (150 g) and chop it finely. Grate the cheese (50 g). Measure 500 g of minced meat, 300 g of passata, 500 ml of milk, 40 g of butter and 40 g of flour. Get out a pot for the potatoes, a large frying pan, a saucepan for the béchamel and a 22 x 30 cm baking dish greased with butter.
Put the potato slices in boiling salted water and cook for 5–6 minutes, until half-cooked (still firm when pricked with a fork). Drain them and let them cool.
Heat the oven to 180°C. Put the frying pan over medium heat, add the onion and a little butter (from the 40 g) and sauté for 3–4 minutes, until translucent.

Add the minced meat, salt and pepper and brown it for 6–8 minutes, breaking it up with the spoon, until no pink remains. Add the passata and simmer over low heat for 10 minutes, until the sauce thickens. Tip: the meat sauce should be fairly thick so the moussaka isn't watery.

For the béchamel, melt the remaining butter in a saucepan over low heat. Add the flour and whisk for 1 minute. Pour in the milk gradually, stirring continuously, then simmer for 5–6 minutes, until it thickens and coats the back of the spoon. Take it off the heat.
Let the béchamel cool for 3–4 minutes, then add the 2 beaten eggs, stirring quickly. Add a little salt.
Arrange half of the potatoes in the dish, then all of the meat sauce, then the remaining potatoes.
Pour the béchamel over the potatoes, smooth it out and sprinkle with the grated cheese.
Bake at 180°C for 40 minutes, until the surface is golden and the béchamel has set. Let the moussaka rest for 10–15 minutes before cutting so it holds together. It keeps in the fridge for 3 days.

60.b: Vegetables rich in water and fibre, plus protein from the meat.
60.a: Contains: Milk. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Heat the oven to 190°C. Wash the zucchini (4, 800 g) and cut them in half lengthways. Peel the onion (100 g) and chop it finely. Cut the tomatoes (100 g) into small dice. Grate the mozzarella (100 g). Rinse the rice (50 g). Measure 300 g of minced meat and 15 ml of oil. Get out a baking dish greased with oil, a spoon and a frying pan.
Scoop out the centre of the zucchini with a spoon, leaving walls about 1 cm thick. Finely chop the scooped-out flesh and set it aside. Tip: don't scoop too deep, so they don't break.
Heat the oil in the frying pan over medium heat. Add the onion and the chopped zucchini flesh and sauté for 4–5 minutes.
Add the minced meat, salt and pepper and cook for 5–6 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains. Add the tomatoes and the rinsed rice, stir and cook for 2 minutes. Take it off the heat.
Arrange the hollowed zucchini in the dish. Fill them with the meat mixture, pressing down gently.
Pour 100 ml of water into the bottom of the dish so the rice cooks in the steam. Cover the dish with aluminium foil.

Bake for 25 minutes covered, then remove the foil, sprinkle with the mozzarella and bake for another 10–15 minutes (35–40 in total), until the cheese melts and turns golden and the zucchini are tender. Check that the rice is cooked.
Let it rest for 5 minutes and serve warm. It keeps in the fridge in a closed container for 2–3 days.

103.b: Lycopene and vitamin C from the tomatoes.
103.a: Contains: Celery. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Prepare the ingredients: peel and finely chop the 100 g of onion (about 0.5 cm cubes) and crush or finely chop the 2 garlic cloves. Measure out 800 g of diced tomatoes, 500 ml of stock and 15 ml of oil, then get out a 3-litre pot, a wooden spoon and an immersion blender or food processor.
Heat the 15 ml of oil in the pot over medium heat for about 1 minute, until it moves easily across the bottom of the pot.
Add the onion and cook for about 3–4 minutes, stirring often, until soft and translucent. Don't let it brown too much, or it will turn bitter.
Add the garlic and stir for another 30–40 seconds, until you can smell it. Tip: garlic burns quickly, so don't leave it unattended.
Add the 800 g of diced tomatoes and the 500 ml of stock. Stir well and add a little salt and pepper along with them.
Cover the pot with the lid slightly ajar and simmer over low-medium heat for about 20 minutes, until the tomatoes are very soft and the soup has a mildly sweet aroma. Stir from time to time.

Take the pot off the heat and let the soup cool for 2–3 minutes. Blend it right in the pot with the immersion blender until smooth and even. Tip: if you use a regular blender, fill the jar only halfway and hold the lid down with a towel, because hot liquid splatters.

Put the pot back on low heat and add the basil leaves, torn by hand. If you want a creamier soup, add the 50 ml of cooking cream too and stir for 1–2 minutes, without letting it boil hard. Taste and adjust with salt and pepper.
Serve the soup hot in bowls, with a few basil leaves on top. It keeps in the fridge in a covered container for 3–4 days; reheat it over low heat.

104.n: Potato soup with sour cream (ciorbă de cartofi)
104.b: Potassium and vitamin C; nourishing and inexpensive.
104.a: Contains: Milk. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Prepare the vegetables: peel the 600 g of potatoes and cut them into 2 cm cubes; peel the 100 g of carrot and slice it into thin 0.5 cm rounds; peel the 100 g of onion and chop it finely. Measure out 1.2 l of water, 200 ml of borș and 100 g of sour cream, then wash the dill and chop it finely. Get out a 3–4 litre pot.
Put the 1.2 l of cold water, the onion, the carrot and the potatoes in the pot. Add a teaspoon of salt and set the pot over high heat until it comes to a boil.

When the water boils, reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer the vegetables, with the lid slightly ajar, for about 20 minutes, until the potatoes and carrots can easily be mashed with a fork. If foam forms on the surface, skim it off with a spoon.
Separately, heat the 200 ml of borș in a small saucepan over medium heat until it comes to its first boil. Tip: borș that has been boiled separately no longer tastes raw and won't curdle in the soup.
Pour the hot borș into the pot in a thin stream, stirring gently. Let the soup simmer over low heat for another 3–5 minutes so the flavors come together.
Taste the soup and adjust with salt and pepper as you like. If it is too sour, add a little hot water; if it is too bland, add a bit more salt, little by little.
Put the sour cream in a small bowl and add 2–3 spoonfuls of the hot soup, stirring, so it warms up gradually. Tip: this way the sour cream won't curdle when it meets the hot soup.

Serve the soup hot in bowls, with a spoonful of sour cream in each and the chopped dill on top. It keeps in the fridge in a covered container for 2–3 days; reheat without boiling hard, adding the sour cream at serving time.

105.a: No major allergens in the basic ingredients; check the labels of the products you use.
s: Wash the 300 g of tomatoes and cut them into slices or thick wedges about 1 cm thick, then into smaller pieces if they are large. Peel the 40 g of onion and slice it into very thin half-moons. Wash the parsley, shake it dry and chop it finely. Get out a large bowl or a deep plate.
Put the tomatoes in the bowl and add the onion on top. Tip: if you find the onion too sharp, soak it in cold water for 5 minutes and drain it well before using.
Drizzle with the 15 ml of oil and the 5 ml of vinegar, then sprinkle with a pinch of salt, about the tip of a teaspoon.
Add the chopped parsley and toss gently with two spoons so the tomatoes don't get crushed. Taste and add more salt or pepper if needed.

Serve immediately, as a side dish or a snack, with fresh bread for mopping up the juices. Tip: the salad doesn't keep well, because the tomatoes release water; if there are leftovers, keep them in the fridge for 1 day at most.

106.a: Contains: Milk, Eggs, Mustard. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Prepare the vegetables: remove the outer leaves of the cabbage and wash the 300 g of cabbage; peel the 100 g of carrot. Get out a large bowl, a coarse grater or a very sharp knife, and a small bowl for the dressing.
Cut or shred the cabbage into very thin strips, 2–3 mm wide, and put them in the large bowl. Grate the carrot on the coarse side of the grater and add it to the cabbage.

Sprinkle a small pinch of salt over the vegetables and rub them with your hands for about 1 minute, until they soften a little. Tip: if the cabbage releases a lot of liquid, drain it lightly before adding the dressing.
In the small bowl, stir the 80 g of yogurt, the 40 g of mayonnaise and the 10 ml of lemon juice together with a spoon until you get a smooth dressing. Taste and add salt and pepper.
Pour the dressing over the vegetables and mix well, until all the strips are evenly coated.

Cover the bowl and put it in the fridge for at least 10 minutes, so the flavors come together and the cabbage stays crunchy. Serve cold, as a side for grilled meat or sandwiches. It keeps in the fridge in a covered container for 2 days.

107.b: Beetroot provides folate and natural nitrates.
107.a: Contains: Milk. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Take out the 400 g of cooked beetroot and, if it isn't peeled yet, remove the skin. Peel the 2 garlic cloves and wash the dill. Get ready a coarse grater, a large bowl and a small bowl. Tip: wear gloves or lay a sheet of foil on the counter, because beetroot stains.
Grate the beetroot on the coarse side of the grater and put it in the large bowl.
Crush the garlic with a garlic press or chop it very finely, and chop the dill finely.
In the small bowl, mix the 150 g of yogurt with the garlic, the dill and a pinch of salt until smooth.
Pour the dressing over the beetroot and mix gently, until all the beetroot is coated. Taste and adjust with salt and pepper.
Drizzle the 15 ml of oil on top, without stirring again. Serve cold, as a salad or a side dish. It keeps in the fridge in a covered container for 2–3 days.

108.b: Calcium and protein from the mozzarella, lycopene from the tomatoes.
108.a: Contains: Milk. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Take the tomatoes and mozzarella out of the fridge about 15 minutes ahead so they taste better. Wash the 250 g of tomatoes and dry them. Drain the 125 g of mozzarella from its whey and pat it lightly dry with a paper towel. Wash the basil leaves. Get out a large plate and a very sharp knife.
Slice the tomatoes about 0.5 cm thick with a very sharp knife so they don't get crushed.
Slice the mozzarella to the same thickness, about 0.5 cm.

Arrange the slices on the plate, alternating tomato and mozzarella and overlapping them slightly, in a circle or in a row. Tip: salt only the tomatoes, not the mozzarella, so it doesn't release water.
Tuck basil leaves between the slices and scatter some on top. Sprinkle with salt and pepper to taste.
Drizzle with the 15 ml of olive oil and the 5 ml of balsamic vinegar. Serve immediately, at room temperature, as a starter or a light salad.

109.n: Salată de boeuf (Romanian chicken and vegetable salad)
109.b: Protein from the chicken and a variety of vegetables.
109.a: Contains: Eggs, Mustard. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Prepare the vegetables: wash the 400 g of potatoes and the 200 g of carrots without peeling them yet, so they don't lose their flavor in the water. Get out two pots (one 3-litre, one 2-litre), a cutting board, a knife, a large bowl and a colander. Measure out 150 g of peas, 150 g of pickled cucumbers, 250 g of chicken breast, 150 g of mayonnaise and 10 g of mustard.

Put the potatoes and carrots in a pot with enough cold water to cover them and add a teaspoon of salt. Boil them over medium heat, counting from the moment the water boils, for about 20–25 minutes, until easily pierced with a fork.

In the other pot, boil the chicken breast in salted water over medium-low heat for about 20 minutes, until it is no longer pink in the middle and reaches 75°C inside. If you use frozen peas, boil them separately for 3–5 minutes in boiling water and drain them.
Drain the vegetables and the chicken and let them cool completely, at least 30 minutes. Tip: if you cut them while warm, the salad turns mushy and the mayonnaise melts.
Peel the potatoes and carrots. Cut the potatoes, carrots and chicken into cubes of about 0.5–1 cm and put them in the large bowl.
Drain the 150 g of pickled cucumbers well and cut them into cubes of the same size. Add them to the bowl, together with the 150 g of peas.
Add the 150 g of mayonnaise and the 10 g of mustard. Mix gently with a large spoon until all the ingredients are coated, without mashing them.
Taste and adjust with salt and pepper. If you want a stronger flavor, add a little more mustard.

Cover the bowl and keep the salad in the fridge for at least 1–2 hours so the flavors come together. Serve cold, as a starter or on slices of bread. It keeps in the fridge in a covered container for 2–3 days.

110.a: No major allergens in the basic ingredients; check the labels of the products you use.
s: Rinse the 200 g of lentils under cold running water in a colander and pick out any little stones. Wash the 150 g of tomatoes, the 100 g of cucumbers and the 30 g of spring onions. Get out a 2-litre pot, a large bowl and a cutting board.
Put the lentils in the pot and cover them with cold water, about three times their volume. Add a little salt and set the pot over high heat until it comes to a boil.
Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer the lentils for about 15–20 minutes, until tender but not falling apart. Tip: taste them after 15 minutes; they should be soft but hold their shape.
Drain the lentils in a colander and rinse them briefly with cold water to stop the cooking. Let them drain well and cool for a few minutes.
Cut the tomatoes and cucumbers into cubes of about 1 cm and the spring onions into thin rounds. Put them in the large bowl.
Add the cooled lentils on top of the vegetables.
Drizzle with the 15 ml of olive oil and the 15 ml of lemon juice. Add salt and pepper to taste and toss gently.
Serve at room temperature or cold. It keeps in the fridge in a covered container for 2–3 days.

111.b: Vitamin K and calcium; healthy fats from the walnuts.
111.a: Contains: Milk, Tree nuts. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Put the 100 g of arugula in a bowl of cold water and rinse it well, then drain it and dry it in a salad spinner or between two clean towels. Wash the 150 g of cherry tomatoes. Get out a large bowl and a vegetable peeler.
Cut the cherry tomatoes in half and break the walnuts into large pieces, by hand or with a knife.
Using the vegetable peeler, shave thin flakes from the 30 g of Parmesan, drawing it along the length of the piece.
Put the arugula in the large bowl and add the tomatoes, walnuts and Parmesan. Tip: don't add the dressing until you serve, so the arugula doesn't wilt.
Drizzle with the 15 ml of olive oil and the 10 ml of balsamic vinegar. Add a little pepper and toss gently, with your hands or two spoons.
Serve immediately, as a standalone salad or as a side for grilled meat.

112.a: Contains: Milk, Eggs. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Wash the 100 g of spinach and drain it well; if the stems are thick, trim them. Crumble the 30 g of feta with a fork. Crack the 4 eggs into a bowl, add salt and pepper and beat them with a fork until the whites and yolks are combined. Get out a 24 cm non-stick frying pan.
Heat the 10 ml of oil in the pan over medium heat for about 1 minute.
Add the spinach to the pan and cook for about 2 minutes, stirring, until it wilts and shrinks.
Pour the beaten eggs over the spinach, spreading them evenly across the bottom of the pan. Reduce the heat to low.

Cook for about 2–3 minutes without stirring, until the edges set. With a spatula, gently pull the edges toward the center, letting the liquid egg run out to the edges. Tip: low heat makes the omelette fluffy, not dry.
Sprinkle the feta over half of the omelette and cook for another 1–2 minutes, until the eggs are completely set and no longer runny.
Fold the omelette in half with the spatula and leave it for 30 seconds. Divide it into two portions and serve immediately, warm, with toast.

113.b: Energy from the flour; the berries add vitamin C.
113.a: Contains: Gluten, Milk, Eggs. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Get all the ingredients ready: measure out 200 g of flour, 300 ml of milk, 30 g of sugar, 10 g of baking powder and 100 g of berries, if using. Melt the 30 g of butter in a small pan over very low heat or in the microwave, then let it cool slightly. Set out two bowls, a whisk and a non-stick frying pan.
In a large bowl, whisk the flour, sugar and baking powder together until evenly combined.
In the other bowl, lightly beat the 2 eggs with the 300 ml of milk until combined. Add the melted, cooled butter and mix again.

Pour the liquid mixture into the dry one and stir briefly with a spatula, just until the dry flour disappears. The batter should stay a bit lumpy. Tip: don't overmix the batter, so the pancakes stay fluffy.
Let the batter rest for 5 minutes, while the baking powder starts to work. Meanwhile, heat the pan over medium heat and grease it very lightly with a little butter.
Pour a large spoonful of batter into the pan for each pancake, leaving 3–4 cm between them. If you're using berries, sprinkle a few over each pancake now.
Cook for about 2–3 minutes, until bubbles appear on the surface and the edges look dry. Flip with a spatula and cook for another 1–2 minutes, until golden brown.
Repeat with the rest of the batter, greasing the pan as needed. Keep the pancakes warm, covered with a clean towel or in an oven at 80°C.
Serve warm, with the berries on top. They keep in the fridge in a covered container for 2 days; reheat for 20–30 seconds in the microwave or in a pan.

114.b: Protein and fats that keep you full.
114.a: Contains: Eggs. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Get out a 24–26 cm non-stick frying pan, a spatula and two plates. Cut the 80 g of bacon into 2 cm wide strips. Wash the 100 g of tomatoes and cut them into slices or quarters. Crack each egg into a small bowl or cup, so you can check that the yolk is intact and keep any shell out.
Put the bacon in the cold pan so it releases its fat gradually, then heat the pan over medium heat.
Brown the bacon for about 4–5 minutes, turning it from time to time, until it is golden and crisp at the edges. Remove it to a paper towel.

Leave about a tablespoon of fat in the pan; if too little is left, add the 10 ml of oil. Reduce the heat to medium-low. Tip: don't let the pan get too hot, so the white doesn't burn while the yolk stays raw.
Gently slide the eggs into the pan, one at a time, from the small bowl. Sprinkle with a little salt and pepper.
Cook the eggs for about 3–4 minutes, until the white is completely white and set and the yolk is as runny as you like. For a firmer yolk, cover the pan with a lid for 1–2 minutes.
Lift the eggs onto the plates with the spatula and add the bacon and tomatoes alongside. Serve immediately, warm, with bread.

115.a: Contains: Gluten, Peanuts. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Take out the 2 slices of bread (80 g), the 30 g of peanut butter and the banana (120 g). Peel the banana. Get ready a toaster or a dry frying pan, a knife for spreading and a plate.
Toast the bread slices in the toaster for 2–3 minutes, until golden brown and crisp. If you don't have a toaster, toast them in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 1–2 minutes on each side.
Slice the banana into rounds about 0.5 cm thick.

Spread the 30 g of peanut butter, divided between the two slices, over the still-warm bread with a knife, so it softens slightly and spreads easily. Tip: warm bread melts the peanut butter a little and it spreads more easily.
Arrange the banana rounds over the peanut butter, slightly overlapping. Serve immediately, so the bread stays crisp.

116.n: Cottage cheese and tomato open sandwiches
116.b: Protein from the cottage cheese, vitamin C from the tomatoes.
116.a: Contains: Gluten, Milk. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Take out the 4 slices of bread (160 g) and the 150 g of cottage cheese. Wash the 150 g of tomatoes and cut them into 0.5 cm slices. Wash the 10 g of spring onion, trim the ends and chop it finely. Get ready a toaster or a frying pan, a knife for spreading and a plate.
Toast the bread slices for 2–3 minutes, until lightly browned and crisp. If you use a frying pan, toast them without oil over medium heat for 1–2 minutes on each side.
Let the bread cool for 1 minute. Tip: if the cottage cheese is very watery, drain it in a sieve for a few minutes.
Add a little salt and pepper to the cottage cheese and stir it with a fork. Spread it evenly over the 4 slices of bread.
Lay the tomato slices over the cheese and sprinkle with the chopped spring onion. Add a little salt and pepper on top.
Serve immediately, so the bread stays crisp.

117.b: Protein from the eggs and energy from the potatoes.
117.a: Contains: Eggs. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Peel the 300 g of potatoes and cut them into thin 2–3 mm slices. Peel the 100 g of onion and slice it into thin half-moons. Crack the 4 eggs into a large bowl, add a pinch of salt and beat them with a fork. Get out a 24 cm non-stick frying pan with a lid and a flat plate of the same size or larger.
Heat the 30 ml of oil in the pan over medium heat for about 1 minute.

Add the potatoes and onion, sprinkle with salt and stir well. Cook over medium-low heat, covered, for 12–15 minutes, stirring from time to time, until the potatoes are soft when you press them with a fork, without browning too much.
Transfer the potatoes and onion to a colander or onto a paper towel and let them drain of oil for 1–2 minutes. Leave about a tablespoon of oil in the pan.
Add the potatoes and onion to the beaten eggs and mix gently to coat them. Taste the raw egg mixture and adjust the salt.
Heat the pan over medium heat and pour in the whole mixture, then reduce the heat to low. Cook for about 6–8 minutes, until the bottom is golden and the edges are set.
Place the plate over the pan, flip them over quickly in one confident motion, then slide the omelette back into the pan, raw side down. Tip: use oven mitts, because the pan is hot.
Cook for about 3 more minutes, until the other side is golden too and the egg inside is completely set, with no liquid left.
Let the omelette rest for 2–3 minutes, then cut it into wedges. Serve warm or at room temperature. It keeps in the fridge in a covered container for 2 days.

118.a: Contains: Milk, Tree nuts. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Get out two bowls, the 300 g of yogurt, the 30 g of walnuts and the 20 g of honey. Break the walnuts into small pieces, by hand or with a knife on a cutting board.
Divide the yogurt between the two bowls, about 150 g in each. Smooth the surface with the back of a spoon.
Sprinkle the broken walnuts over each portion. Tip: toast the walnuts for 2–3 minutes in a dry pan over low heat to bring out more flavor.
Drizzle the honey, 10 g per bowl, in a thin stream over each portion.
Serve immediately, chilled, as breakfast or a light dessert.

119.b: Protein and choline from the eggs.
119.a: Contains: Eggs, Mustard. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Take out the 6 hard-boiled eggs, peel them under cold running water and pat them dry. Wash the 10 g of spring onion and chop it very finely. Get ready a knife, a small bowl, a spoon and a plate.
Cut each boiled egg lengthwise into two halves with a very sharp knife.
Carefully scoop out the yolks with a teaspoon and put them in the small bowl. Arrange the whites on the plate, hollow side up.
Mash the yolks with a fork until they turn into a fine crumble with no lumps.
Add the 60 g of mayonnaise, the 10 g of mustard and the spring onion. Mix until you get a smooth cream. Taste and add salt and pepper.
Fill the egg whites with the cream, using a teaspoon or a piping bag. Tip: you can snip a corner off a plastic bag to fill them more easily.
Sprinkle paprika on top. Serve cold, as a starter. They keep in the fridge, covered with cling film, for 1 day at most.

120.n: Cream cheese and cucumber open sandwiches
120.b: A light snack with calcium and hydration.
120.a: Contains: Gluten, Milk. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Take out the 4 slices of bread (160 g), the 120 g of cream cheese and the 100 g of cucumbers. Wash the cucumbers and the dill. Slice the cucumbers into rounds about 3 mm thick and chop the dill finely. Get ready a toaster or a frying pan, a knife for spreading and a plate.
Lightly toast the bread slices for 1–2 minutes, until browned and slightly crisp. If you use a frying pan, toast them without oil over medium heat.
Let the bread cool for 1–2 minutes. Tip: warm bread melts the cream cheese, so wait for it to cool a little.
Spread the 120 g of cream cheese over the slices in an even layer with a knife, almost to the edges.
Arrange the cucumber rounds over the cream cheese, slightly overlapping, and sprinkle with the chopped dill. Add a little pepper.
Cut each open sandwich in half or into quarters, as you prefer. Serve immediately, as a starter or a snack.

121.b: Calcium and protein from the feta, lycopene from the tomatoes.
121.a: Contains: Milk. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Preheat the oven to 200°C, using the top-and-bottom heat setting, and place the rack in the middle. Wash the 250 g of cherry tomatoes and dry them. Peel the 2 garlic cloves and slice them thinly. Get out a small ovenproof dish, about 20 cm.
Place the 200 g of feta in the center of the dish, in one whole piece.
Arrange the cherry tomatoes around the feta, whole, and scatter the garlic slices between them.
Drizzle the 20 ml of olive oil over the tomatoes and the feta. Sprinkle with oregano and a little pepper. Tip: feta is already salty, so don't add any salt.
Put the dish in the hot oven and bake for 15–20 minutes, until the tomatoes have burst and are soft, and the feta is golden and slightly softened at the edges.
Take the dish out and let it cool a little for 3–5 minutes.

Serve hot, straight from the dish, with fresh bread or slices of toast. You can crush the tomatoes with a fork and mix them with the feta to make a sauce. It keeps in the fridge in a covered container for 1–2 days.

122.b: Protein and calcium in a quick snack.
122.a: Contains: Milk. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Take out the 8 slices of ham (160 g), the 120 g of cream cheese and the 80 g of pickled cucumbers. Wash the parsley and chop it finely. Drain the pickles and cut them into thin strips about 5 cm long. Get out a plate, a knife and a cutting board.
Lay a slice of ham flat on the cutting board, with no wrinkles.
Spread about 15 g of cream cheese over each slice with a knife, in a thin layer, almost to the edges.
Place a strip of pickled cucumber at one end of the slice, crosswise.
Roll the ham up tightly, starting from the end with the pickle, until you have a roll. Tip: press gently as you roll so it doesn't come undone.
Repeat with the remaining slices, then put the rolls in the fridge for 10 minutes to firm up.
Cut each roll into 3–4 pieces with a very sharp knife and arrange them on the plate. Sprinkle with parsley and serve cold. They keep in the fridge, covered, for 1–2 days.

123.b: Fiber and vitamin A, lighter than store-bought chips.
123.a: No major allergens in the basic ingredients; check the labels of the products you use.
s: Preheat the oven to 170°C, fan setting if you have one, and line two baking trays with parchment paper. Wash the 150 g of sweet potatoes, the 150 g of carrots and the 150 g of beetroot well and peel them. Get out a large bowl. Tip: wear gloves for the beetroot, because it stains.
Slice the vegetables very thinly, about 2 mm, with a very sharp knife or a slicer.
Pat the slices dry with a clean kitchen towel; moisture keeps them from getting crisp.
Put the slices in a large bowl, add the 20 ml of oil and a pinch of salt, and toss well with your hands until all the slices are lightly coated.
Arrange the slices on the trays in a single layer, without overlapping. Keep the beetroot on a separate tray. Tip: if the trays are crowded, the vegetables steam instead of getting crisp.
Bake for 25–30 minutes, checking after 20 minutes. Turn the slices halfway through and remove any that brown faster.
Take the trays out when the edges are golden and the slices are crisp, then let the chips cool on the tray for 5–10 minutes; they firm up as they cool.
Serve as a snack. They keep in an airtight container at room temperature for 2–3 days.

124.n: Roasted walnuts with honey and rosemary
124.a: Contains: Tree nuts. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Preheat the oven to 160°C, using the top-and-bottom heat setting. Line a baking tray with parchment paper. Measure out 200 g of walnuts, 20 g of honey and a small sprig of rosemary; wash the rosemary, dry it and chop the leaves very finely. Get out a large bowl.
Spread the walnuts on the tray in a single layer.
Roast the walnuts for 8 minutes, until they smell fragrant and turn lightly golden. Tip: walnuts burn quickly, so don't leave them unattended during the last few minutes.
Take the tray out of the oven and immediately put the hot walnuts in the large bowl.
Add the 20 g of honey, the chopped rosemary and a pinch of salt. Stir vigorously with a spoon until the walnuts are evenly coated.
Spread the walnuts back onto the parchment paper and let them cool completely, 10–15 minutes; they will firm up. Break apart any pieces that have stuck together.
Serve as a snack or with cheeses. They keep in a closed jar at room temperature for about 1 week.

125.a: No major allergens in the basic ingredients; check the labels of the products you use.
s: Preheat the oven to 230°C and place the rack in the middle. Wash the 600 g of peppers and dry them. Line a baking tray with parchment paper. Peel the 2 garlic cloves and crush or finely chop them. Get out a bowl with a lid or a heat-resistant plastic bag.
Place the whole peppers on the tray, on the parchment paper, without cutting them.
Roast them for 25–30 minutes, turning them every 8–10 minutes, until the skin blackens in places and puffs up, and the peppers are soft.

Carefully take the peppers out and immediately put them in a bowl covered with a lid or in a sealed bag. Leave them for 10 minutes so the steam loosens the skin. Tip: the peppers shouldn't cool down completely before you peel them.
Peel off the skin and remove the stems and seeds, holding the peppers with your fingers. You can use a spoon to scrape off any remaining skin; don't rinse them, so they don't lose their flavor.
Cut the peppers into wide strips and put them in a bowl. Add the garlic, the 30 ml of oil and the 10 ml of vinegar. Sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Mix gently and let them marinate for at least 15 minutes at room temperature. Serve as a starter, with bread, or as a side dish. They keep in the fridge in a covered container for 3–4 days.

126.a: Contains: Gluten. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Preheat the oven to 200°C and line a large baking tray with parchment paper. Drain and rinse the 400 g of cooked chickpeas, then dry them well with a towel. Peel the 80 g of onion and cut it into large pieces. Peel the 2 garlic cloves. Wash the parsley and chop it roughly. Get out a food processor and a bowl.
Put the chickpeas, onion, garlic, parsley and cumin in the food processor. Add a little salt.
Pulse in short bursts until you get a coarse paste that holds together when you squeeze it in your hand. Don't blend it until smooth. Tip: if the mixture is too wet, add a little more flour.
Transfer the mixture to the bowl and add the 30 g of flour. Mix well with a spoon.
With slightly dampened hands, shape the mixture into about 12 balls the size of a walnut and flatten them a little. Place them on the tray, 2 cm apart.
Brush or drizzle the falafel with the 15 ml of oil, on both sides.
Bake for 25 minutes, turning the balls halfway through, until they are golden and crisp at the edges.

Take out the tray and let the falafel cool for 5 minutes so they firm up. Serve warm, with salad and a yogurt sauce. They keep in the fridge in a covered container for 3 days; reheat them in the oven to keep them crisp.

127.b: Monounsaturated fats, potassium and vitamin E.
127.a: No major allergens in the basic ingredients; check the labels of the products you use.
s: Wash the 100 g of tomatoes and cut them in half. Scoop out the seeds with a spoon and dice the tomatoes into small 0.5 cm cubes. Peel the 50 g of red onion and chop it very finely. Wash the cilantro and chop it finely. Get out a medium bowl and a fork.
Cut each avocado in half lengthwise, working around the pit. Twist the halves to separate them and remove the pit.
Scoop out the flesh with a spoon and put it in the bowl. Mash it with the fork to the texture you want, either smooth or chunky. Tip: if you keep the pit in the bowl, the avocado browns more slowly.
Add the red onion, the tomatoes and the chopped cilantro. Mix gently.
Drizzle with the 15 ml of lime juice and add salt to taste. Stir and taste; adjust with more salt or lime juice.
Serve immediately, with chips, raw vegetables or tortillas. It keeps in the fridge, covered with cling film pressed directly against the surface, for 1 day at most.

128.b: Protein and calcium from the yogurt.
128.a: Contains: Milk. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Wash the 150 g of cucumbers and grate them on the coarse side of the grater, leaving the peel on if it is thin. Peel the 2 garlic cloves. Wash the dill and chop it finely. Get out a bowl, a sieve, a clean kitchen towel and a garlic press.
Put the grated cucumber in a clean towel or a sieve and squeeze it well to remove all the liquid. Tip: if the liquid stays in, the sauce turns watery.
Put the 300 g of yogurt in the large bowl and add the drained cucumber.
Crush the garlic and add it to the bowl, then stir well with a spoon until smooth.
Add the 15 ml of olive oil, the chopped dill and salt to taste. Stir again.

Cover the bowl and keep the sauce in the fridge for at least 30 minutes so the flavors come together. Serve cold, with grilled meat, vegetables or bread. It keeps in the fridge in a covered container for 2–3 days.

129.a: Contains: Milk, Tree nuts. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Wash the 50 g of basil, dry it well with a towel and pick the leaves off the stems. Peel the garlic clove. Grate the 40 g of Parmesan on the fine side of the grater. Measure out 40 g of walnuts and 80 ml of olive oil. Get out a blender or food processor and a clean jar.
Put the basil, garlic, walnuts and grated Parmesan in the blender.
Add about half of the 80 ml of olive oil to help the blending. Tip: save a little oil to cover the pesto.
Blend in short pulses, stopping from time to time to scrape down the sides with a spatula, until a coarse paste forms.
Add the rest of the oil in a thin stream with the blender running, and blend until you have a smooth paste. Taste and add a little salt if needed; the Parmesan is already salty.

Spoon the pesto into the clean jar and press it down gently with a spoon to remove air. Cover the surface with a thin layer of oil and close the jar. It keeps in the fridge for 5–7 days; add a fresh layer of oil after each use.

130.a: No major allergens in the basic ingredients; check the labels of the products you use.
s: Peel the 100 g of onion and chop it finely, into cubes of about 0.5 cm. Peel the 2 garlic cloves and chop them finely. Measure out 800 g of diced tomatoes and 30 ml of olive oil. Wash the basil and tear it by hand. Get out a 3-litre saucepan and a wooden spoon.
Heat the 30 ml of olive oil in the saucepan over medium heat for about 1 minute.
Add the onion and cook for 4–5 minutes, stirring often, until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic and stir for 30–40 seconds, until fragrant. Tip: don't let the garlic brown, because it turns bitter.
Add the 800 g of diced tomatoes, a pinch of salt and some pepper. Stir well.
Simmer the sauce over low heat, with the lid slightly ajar, for about 20 minutes, stirring from time to time, until it thickens and loses its raw tomato flavor.
Add the basil and stir. Taste and adjust the salt. If you want a smoother sauce, blend it with an immersion blender.
Serve warm, with pasta, rice or meat. It keeps in the fridge in a covered container for 4–5 days, or in the freezer for up to 3 months.

131.a: No major allergens in the basic ingredients; check the labels of the products you use.
s: Preheat the oven to 220°C. Wash the 600 g of eggplants, dry them and prick them a few times with a fork so they don't burst. Line a baking tray with parchment paper. Peel the 50 g of onion and chop it very finely. Get out a bowl, a sieve and a cutting board.
Place the whole eggplants on the tray and roast them for about 30 minutes, turning them halfway through, until the skin is charred and the eggplants are very soft when pressed.
Take the eggplants out and let them cool for 5–10 minutes, until you can hold them in your hand.
Peel the eggplants, holding them with your fingers, and cut off the stems. Put the flesh in a sieve.
Let the flesh drain for 10–15 minutes, pressing lightly with a spoon. Tip: draining removes the bitterness and makes the salad creamier.
Chop the flesh finely on a cutting board with a wooden or plastic knife until you get a smooth paste. Tip: avoid a metal knife, which can darken the eggplant.
Put the paste in a bowl and add the onion, the 30 ml of oil, the 10 ml of lemon juice and salt. Mix well until creamy. Taste and adjust.
Serve cold or at room temperature, on fresh bread. It keeps in the fridge in a covered container for 2 days.

132.a: No major allergens in the basic ingredients; check the labels of the products you use.
s: Get out a 1.5-litre pitcher, a cup, a spoon and a juicer. Measure out 80 g of sugar, 1 l of water and 200 ml of lemon juice, freshly squeezed or store-bought. Wash the mint leaves. Get the ice cubes ready.
Heat about 200 ml of the measured water until hot but not boiling, and pour it into the pitcher.
Add the 80 g of sugar to the hot water and stir for 1–2 minutes, until it dissolves completely and you can no longer see any crystals.
Pour the 200 ml of lemon juice into the pitcher, then add the rest of the cold water. Stir well.
Taste the lemonade. If it is too sour, add a little sugar; if it is too sweet, add a little water. Tip: the flavor gets diluted when you add the ice, so make it a bit stronger.
Put the pitcher in the fridge for 15–20 minutes. Serve in glasses with ice cubes and mint leaves. It keeps in the fridge for 2–3 days.

133.n: Ginger tea with lemon and honey
133.b: Ginger aids digestion; lemon provides vitamin C.
133.a: No major allergens in the basic ingredients; check the labels of the products you use.
s: Wash the 20 g of ginger and peel it by scraping off the thin skin with a small spoon. Slice it into thin 2–3 mm slices. Measure out 500 ml of water, 30 ml of lemon juice and 20 g of honey. Get out a small saucepan, a sieve and two cups.
Put the water and ginger in the saucepan and heat over high heat until it comes to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 8 minutes, with the lid on, until the water turns slightly golden and the ginger smells strong.
Take the saucepan off the heat and strain the tea into the two cups through the sieve.
Let the tea cool for 2–3 minutes. Tip: don't add honey to boiling liquid, so it keeps its aroma.
Add the 30 ml of lemon juice and the honey (10 g in each cup) and stir until dissolved. Serve warm. It keeps in the fridge in a covered container for 1–2 days; warm it gently before serving.

134.a: Contains: Milk. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Get out a small saucepan, a whisk or a spoon, two cups, 500 ml of milk, 20 g of cocoa powder and 20 g of sugar. Put the cocoa and sugar in a small bowl.

Pour about 50 ml of the milk over the cocoa and sugar and stir vigorously with the spoon or whisk until you get a smooth paste with no lumps. Tip: if the cocoa won't dissolve, whisk it harder or mash the lumps with the back of the spoon.
Pour the rest of the milk (about 450 ml) into the saucepan and add the cocoa paste. Stir well.
Heat over low-medium heat, stirring constantly, for 4–5 minutes, until the milk is hot and starts to steam. Don't let it boil, because the milk will boil over.
Taste and add a little more sugar if needed. Pour into cups and serve hot.

135.b: Vitamins C and A; the yogurt adds protein.
135.a: Contains: Milk. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Get out a blender and two glasses. Peel the 150 g of mango and the 150 g of pineapple and remove the pit or core. Cut them into 2 cm cubes. Measure out 150 g of yogurt, 100 ml of water and a few ice cubes.
Put the mango and pineapple cubes in the blender.
Add the yogurt, water and ice cubes. Tip: put the liquids at the bottom so the blades spin easily.
Close the lid and blend on high speed for 40–60 seconds, until the smoothie is smooth and creamy, with no chunks.
Taste; if it is too thick, add a little water and blend again for 10 seconds. Pour into glasses and serve immediately, cold.

136.a: Contains: Milk. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Get out a small saucepan, a whisk and two cups. Measure out 500 ml of milk, 5 g of turmeric, 3 g of cinnamon, 2 g of ground ginger, 10 g of honey and a small pinch of pepper.
Pour the milk into the saucepan and add the turmeric, cinnamon, ground ginger and pepper.
Whisk so that no lumps remain. Tip: pepper helps the body make use of the turmeric, so don't leave it out.
Heat over low heat, stirring constantly, for 3–4 minutes, until the milk starts to steam. Don't let it come to a boil.
Take the saucepan off the heat and let the milk cool for 1 minute. Add the 10 g of honey and stir until dissolved.
Pour into the two cups, straining if you want a smooth drink, and serve warm, in the evening, before bed.

1.b: Eggs and milk provide protein; fruit adds fiber, vitamin C and antioxidants.
1.a: Gluten (wheat), milk, eggs. May contain traces depending on the products used.
s: Prepare the ingredients: measure out 200 g of flour, 250 ml of milk, 20 g of sugar and 15 ml of oil. Wash the 200 g of fresh fruit, dry it and cut it into small pieces of about 1 cm if it is large. Get out a large bowl, a whisk, a 24 cm non-stick pan and a spatula.
Crack the 2 eggs into the bowl and whisk them for 30 seconds, until combined. Add the 20 g of sugar and mix well.
Pour half of the 250 ml of milk over the eggs and mix. Gradually add the flour, through a sieve or sprinkled in, stirring constantly so that no lumps form.

Add the rest of the milk and the 15 ml of oil and whisk until you get a smooth, fluid batter that pours easily, about like single cream. Tip: let the batter rest for 10 minutes; the crepes will turn out softer and won't tear when flipped.
Heat the pan over medium heat and grease it very lightly with a little oil, spreading it with a paper towel. Take a small ladle of batter (about 60 ml) and pour it into the center of the pan.
Immediately tilt the pan in all directions so the batter covers the bottom evenly in a thin layer.
Cook the crepe for 1–2 minutes, until the edges brown and the surface is no longer shiny. Flip it with the spatula and cook for another 30–60 seconds on the other side, until it has golden spots.

Place the cooked crepe on a plate and repeat with the rest of the batter, greasing the pan only if it starts to stick. Cover the crepes with a lid or a clean towel so they stay soft and warm. Tip: if the first crepe comes out thicker, add 1–2 tablespoons of milk to the batter.
Place one crepe on a plate, put some of the 200 g of fruit in the middle and roll or fold the crepe. Serve immediately, warm. Unfilled crepes keep in the fridge, covered, for 2 days.

2.b: Provides energy; cocoa and dark chocolate contain polyphenols. It is a dessert, not a main source of nutrients.
2.a: Gluten, milk and eggs; the chocolate may contain soy or traces of nuts.
s: Get everything ready first: take the butter and eggs out of the fridge 20 minutes ahead. Weigh out the 200 g of dark chocolate, 120 g of butter, 150 g of sugar, 100 g of flour and 20 g of cocoa. Break the chocolate into small pieces and cut the butter into cubes. Line a 20x20 cm pan with baking paper.
Turn the oven on to 175°C and let it heat up while you prepare the batter.

Put the chocolate and butter in a heatproof bowl set over a pot of gently simmering water (a bain-marie), making sure the bowl does not touch the water. Melt them over low heat, stirring occasionally, for 4–5 minutes, until you have a smooth, glossy cream. Tip: take the bowl off the pot as soon as they have melted so the chocolate doesn't burn.
Take the bowl off the steam and let the mixture cool for 5 minutes; it should be warm, not hot, so it doesn't scramble the eggs.
Add the 150 g of sugar to the melted chocolate and mix well with a whisk for about 1 minute.
Add the 3 eggs one at a time, mixing after each until fully incorporated. The mixture becomes glossy and lighter in color.

Sift the 100 g of flour and the 20 g of cocoa over the mixture. Fold them in with a spatula, using gentle bottom-to-top movements, just until you no longer see traces of flour. Tip: don't overmix, so the brownie stays tender and moist.
Pour the batter into the prepared pan and smooth the surface with the spatula. Tap the pan gently on the counter a few times to release the air bubbles.
Bake at 175°C for about 20–25 minutes. The brownie is done when the edges are firm and a toothpick inserted in the center comes out with a few moist crumbs, not liquid batter.
Take the pan out and let the brownie cool completely in the pan, at least 30 minutes; this lets it set and cut easily. Lift it out using the baking paper and cut it into 8 squares.
Serve at room temperature. It keeps in a closed container, at room temperature or in the fridge, for 3–4 days.

3.b: Dairy products contribute protein and calcium; fruit adds fiber and vitamins.
3.a: Gluten and milk; eggs. The biscuits may contain soy.
s: Prepare the ingredients: take the cream cheese, eggs and yogurt out of the fridge 30 minutes ahead. Weigh out 200 g of biscuits, 100 g of butter, 500 g of cream cheese, 150 g of sugar and 150 g of yogurt. Wash the 150 g of fruit and cut it if it is large. Grease a 20–22 cm springform pan with butter and line the bottom with baking paper.
Turn the oven on to 160°C. Melt the 100 g of butter in a small saucepan over low heat, or in the microwave, in 3–4 bursts of 20 seconds.
Put the biscuits in a thick bag and crush them with a rolling pin until they become fine crumbs, or pulse them briefly in a blender. Tip: the finer the crumbs, the better the base holds together.
Mix the crumbs with the melted butter in a bowl until it resembles wet sand and sticks together when you squeeze it in your fist.
Pour the mixture into the pan and press it firmly onto the bottom and slightly up the sides, using the back of a spoon or the bottom of a glass. Put the pan in the fridge for 10 minutes.
In a large bowl, beat the 500 g of cream cheese with the 150 g of sugar on low speed for about 1–2 minutes, until smooth and free of lumps.

Add the 2 eggs one at a time, mixing only until incorporated, then add the 150 g of yogurt and mix briefly. Tip: don't beat the filling too much after adding the eggs, so it doesn't puff up and crack while baking.
Pour the filling over the cold base and smooth the surface. Tap the pan on the counter 2–3 times to release the air bubbles.
Bake at 160°C for 45–50 minutes. The cheesecake is done when the edges are set and the center jiggles slightly, like gelatin, when you shake the pan.

Turn off the oven, crack the door open and leave the cake inside for 30 minutes, then take it out and let it cool at room temperature. Cover it and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.
Loosen the edges with a knife, open the pan and decorate with the 150 g of fruit. Cut into 8 slices with a knife dipped in warm water. It keeps in the fridge, covered, for 3–4 days.

4.b: Mascarpone and eggs provide protein and calcium; coffee and cocoa contain antioxidant compounds.
4.a: Gluten, milk and eggs; some products may contain soy.
s: Prepare the ingredients: weigh out 200 g of ladyfingers, 250 g of mascarpone, 70 g of sugar and 10 g of cocoa. Brew 200 ml of coffee, let it cool completely and pour it into a wide dish. Get out a rectangular dish of about 20x20 cm, 2 clean, dry bowls and a whisk or mixer. Tip: use very fresh or pasteurized eggs, because the whites and yolks are eaten uncooked.

Separate the 3 eggs: crack each egg and pass the yolk back and forth between the two shell halves, letting the white drip into a bowl. Put the yolks in another bowl. Make sure no trace of yolk gets into the whites, otherwise they won't whip up.
Add the 70 g of sugar to the yolks and beat them with the mixer for 3–4 minutes, until pale, creamy and increased in volume.
Add the 250 g of mascarpone and mix with a spatula or with the mixer on low speed, just until you have a smooth, even cream.
Beat the whites with the clean mixer on high speed for 3–4 minutes, until they form firm peaks that stay on the tip of the whisk when you lift it.
Fold the whites into the mascarpone cream in 2–3 batches, with slow bottom-to-top movements, so it stays airy. Tip: don't stir vigorously, otherwise the foam deflates.

Dip the ladyfingers one at a time in the cold coffee, just 1–2 seconds on each side, and arrange half of them in a layer in the dish. If they stay in the coffee longer, they break apart and turn to mush.
Spread half of the cream over the first layer of ladyfingers, smoothing it evenly. Repeat with the remaining dipped ladyfingers and the rest of the cream.
Cover the dish with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight, so the ladyfingers soften and the cream sets.
Before serving, dust the 10 g of cocoa evenly through a small sieve. Cut into portions and serve cold. It keeps in the fridge, covered, for 2 days.

5.b: Blueberries contain fiber and anthocyanins; milk and egg contribute protein.
s: Prepare the ingredients: take the egg and butter out of the fridge 20 minutes ahead. Weigh out 250 g of flour, 100 g of sugar, 8 g of baking powder, 150 ml of milk, 120 g of blueberries and 80 g of butter. Wash the blueberries and dry them well on a paper towel. Prepare a 12-cup muffin pan, lined with paper liners or greased with butter.
Turn the oven on to 180°C. Melt the 80 g of butter over low heat or in the microwave and let it cool for 5 minutes.
In a large bowl, whisk together the 250 g of flour, the 100 g of sugar and the 8 g of baking powder for a moment, so the baking powder is evenly distributed.
In another bowl, lightly beat the egg with the 150 ml of milk and the melted, cooled butter until combined.

Pour the liquid mixture over the dry ingredients. Mix with a spatula for only 10–15 seconds, until most of the traces of flour disappear; the batter may stay a little lumpy. Tip: don't overmix the batter, so the muffins turn out fluffy.
Add the blueberries and fold them in with 2–3 gentle movements so they don't get crushed.

Divide the batter among the 12 cups with a spoon, filling them about 3/4 full. Tip: if you want to keep the blueberries from sinking, toss them in 1 tablespoon of the measured flour before adding them.
Bake at 180°C for 20–22 minutes, on the middle rack. The muffins are done when they are risen and golden, and a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Take the pan out and leave the muffins in it for 5 minutes, then move them to a rack to cool. Serve them warm or at room temperature. They keep in a closed container for 2–3 days.

6.b: Fruit adds fiber, vitamins and antioxidants; milk contributes calcium.
s: Prepare the ingredients: take the butter out of the fridge 30 minutes ahead and cut it into 1 cm cubes. Weigh out 250 g of flour, 40 g of sugar for the dough and 20 g of sugar for the cream, 20 g of starch, 250 ml of milk and 5 ml of vanilla. Wash the 250 g of fruit, dry it and cut it into slices or small pieces. Grease a 24 cm tart pan with butter.
In a large bowl, put the 250 g of flour, the 40 g of sugar and the 125 g of cubed butter. Rub them together between your fingertips until you get a sandy mixture.

Add the egg and knead briefly, just until the dough comes together into a ball. If it is too dry, add 1 tablespoon of cold water. Tip: don't knead for long, so the dough doesn't turn tough when baked.
Flatten the dough into a disc, wrap it in plastic wrap and leave it in the fridge for 20 minutes. Meanwhile, turn the oven on to 180°C.
Roll out the dough with a rolling pin on a floured surface into a circle about 3 mm thick. Place it in the pan, press it onto the bottom and sides and trim off the excess.
Prick the base with a fork in several places, cover with baking paper and bake at 180°C for 20–25 minutes, until the edges turn golden. Take the tart out and let it cool in the pan.
Prepare the cream: in a saucepan, mix the 20 g of starch with 3–4 tablespoons of the cold milk until no lumps remain. Add the rest of the milk, the 20 g of sugar and the vanilla.
Place the saucepan over medium-low heat and stir constantly for 4–6 minutes, until the cream thickens and coats the back of the spoon. Boil for 1 more minute, then take it off the heat.
Let the cream cool completely, covered with plastic wrap pressed directly onto the surface so a skin doesn't form. Spread the cream over the tart shell and arrange the fruit on top.
Put the tart in the fridge for 30 minutes before serving. Cut into 8 slices. It keeps in the fridge, covered, for 2 days; it is best on the first day.

7.b: Provides protein from the egg and cheese and carbohydrates for energy.
7.a: Gluten, eggs and milk. Check the cheese and the meat products.
s: Prepare the ingredients: weigh out 320 g of spaghetti and 150 g of guanciale. Cut the guanciale into 1 cm thick strips, then into 1 cm pieces. Finely grate the 70 g of pecorino or Parmesan. Put 4 liters of water in a large pot and get out a wide pan.
Put the water over high heat and, when it boils, add about 2 tablespoons of salt. Add the spaghetti and stir during the first minute so it doesn't stick.
Cook the pasta according to the package, about 9–11 minutes, until al dente (firm to the bite). Before draining, reserve 1 cup (about 250 ml) of the cooking water.
Meanwhile, put the guanciale in a cold pan and heat it over low-medium heat. Brown it for 6–8 minutes, stirring, until the fat renders and the pieces turn golden and crisp.

In a bowl, beat the 3 egg yolks and the whole egg with the grated cheese and plenty of freshly ground pepper until you get a thick cream. Tip: don't add salt, the cheese and guanciale are already salty.
Take the pan with the guanciale off the heat and let it cool for 1 minute. The pan must not be too hot, so the eggs don't curdle.
Drain the pasta and add it directly to the pan with the guanciale and the remaining fat. Toss for 30 seconds so it gets coated in the fat.

Pour the egg mixture over the pasta and stir vigorously. Add the pasta water 2–3 tablespoons at a time, until you get a creamy, glossy sauce that coats the spaghetti. Tip: don't put the pan back on the heat; the heat of the pasta is enough to set the sauce without scrambling the eggs.
Serve immediately on warm plates, with freshly ground pepper and a little extra cheese. Eat it right away; it doesn't keep well, because the sauce breaks when reheated.

8.b: The meat provides protein, iron and vitamin B12; tomatoes contain lycopene.
8.a: Gluten; celery; milk if Parmesan is added. Check the pasta and the sauce.
s: Prepare the vegetables: peel the onion (100 g), carrot (80 g) and celery (40 g). Cut them into very small cubes, about 5 mm. Measure out 15 ml of oil, 400 g of ground meat and 400 g of passata. Grate the 30 g of Parmesan, if using. Get out a deep pan or a 3-liter saucepan and a large pot for the pasta.
Heat the 15 ml of oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion, carrot and celery, with a pinch of salt.

Sauté the vegetables for 6–8 minutes, stirring often, until they soften, turn translucent and slightly golden. Tip: when finely diced, the vegetables melt into the sauce and give it sweetness and flavor.

Raise the heat to high and add the 400 g of ground meat. Break it up with a wooden spoon and brown it for 8–10 minutes, until the pink color disappears completely and the water released by the meat evaporates.
Add the 400 g of passata, half a teaspoon of salt and pepper to taste. Mix well.

When the sauce starts to boil, reduce the heat to low. Cover the saucepan with the lid slightly ajar and simmer for 25–30 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes, until the sauce thickens and the oil rises to the surface. If it dries out too much, add 50 ml of water.
12 minutes before the sauce is ready, boil 3 liters of water with 1 tablespoon of salt. Add the 320 g of pasta and cook according to the package, 9–11 minutes, until al dente.

Reserve half a cup of the pasta water, then drain the pasta. Toss the pasta with some of the sauce in the saucepan for 1 minute, adding a little pasta water if needed. Tip: pasta tossed with the sauce in the pan absorbs it better than pasta with sauce poured on top.
Serve on warm plates, with the rest of the sauce on top and the grated Parmesan, if using. The sauce keeps in the fridge, in a closed container, for 3 days, or for 2 months in the freezer.

9.b: Contains protein, iron, calcium and carbohydrates.
9.a: Gluten, milk; possibly eggs in the lasagna sheets and celery in some sauces.
s: Prepare the ingredients: peel the onion (100 g) and cut it into small 5 mm cubes. Weigh out 500 g of ground meat, 500 g of passata, 250 g of lasagna sheets, 40 g of butter, 40 g of flour, 500 ml of milk, 150 g of mozzarella and 50 g of Parmesan. Cut the mozzarella into thin slices or grate it coarsely, and grate the Parmesan. Grease a pan of about 20x30 cm with butter.
Heat a deep pan over medium heat with a little oil or butter. Add the onion and sauté for 4–5 minutes, until it softens and turns translucent.
Add the ground meat, raise the heat and brown it for 8–10 minutes, breaking it up with a wooden spoon, until no trace of pink remains. Add the 500 g of passata, salt and pepper.
Simmer the sauce over low heat for 15–20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it thickens. Take it off the heat.
For the béchamel, melt the 40 g of butter in a saucepan over low heat. Add the 40 g of flour and stir for 1 minute, until it forms a lightly golden paste, but don't brown it.

Add the 500 ml of milk gradually, a little at a time, stirring constantly with a whisk so no lumps form. Simmer over low heat for 4–5 minutes, until it thickens and coats the back of the spoon. Season with a little salt and pepper. Tip: if lumps appear, whisk the sauce vigorously or strain it.
Turn the oven on to 180°C. If the lasagna sheets need pre-boiling, boil them according to the package and drain them.

Begin assembling: spread 2–3 tablespoons of béchamel on the bottom of the pan, then lay down a layer of sheets, a layer of meat sauce and a little béchamel. Repeat the layers 3 times, finishing with béchamel.
Sprinkle the mozzarella and Parmesan evenly on top. Cover the pan with aluminum foil and bake at 180°C for 25 minutes.

Remove the foil and bake for another 10–15 minutes, until the cheese melts, turns golden and bubbles at the edges. Tip: let the lasagna rest for 10–15 minutes before cutting, so the layers hold together.
Cut into 6 portions and serve hot. It keeps in the fridge, covered, for 3 days; it can be reheated in the oven or microwave.

10.b: Chicken provides protein and vitamin B12; rice supplies energy; vegetables add fiber and vitamins.
10.a: In the basic version, it does not necessarily contain any of the 14 allergens. Check the stock and the seasonings.
s: Prepare the ingredients: wash the chicken breast (500 g), dry it with paper towels and cut it into 2 cm cubes. Peel the onion (100 g) and carrot (100 g) and prepare the bell pepper (150 g): finely chop the onion, cut the carrot into thin rounds or 1 cm cubes, and cut the pepper, seeds removed, into 1 cm cubes. Measure out 200 g of rice, 500 ml of water or stock and 15 ml of oil. Get out a pot with a lid or a deep pan.
Put the rice in a sieve and rinse it under cold water for 1 minute, until the water runs almost clear. Drain it well.
Heat the oil in the pot over medium-high heat. Add the chicken, salt and pepper and brown it for 5–6 minutes, stirring occasionally, until lightly colored on all sides.
Add the onion and carrot and cook for 3–4 minutes, stirring, until the onion turns translucent.
Add the bell pepper and the chosen seasonings and cook for 2 more minutes. Tip: add the seasonings (for example paprika or thyme) to the vegetables so they release their flavor into the oil.
Add the rinsed rice and stir for 1 minute, so the grains get coated in oil. Pour in the 500 ml of water or stock and add salt to taste.
When the liquid starts to boil, reduce the heat to low and cover with the lid. Simmer for 15–18 minutes, without lifting the lid, until all the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender.

Check a cube of chicken cut in half: the meat should be white, with no pink, and the internal temperature should be 75°C. If needed, cook for 2–3 more minutes. Tip: don't stir the rice while it cooks, so it doesn't become sticky.

Take the pot off the heat and leave it covered for 5 minutes, to let the rice rest, then fluff it with a fork. Serve hot. It keeps in the fridge, in a closed container, for 2 days; reheat thoroughly until piping hot.

11.b: Potatoes provide potassium and carbohydrates; dairy contributes calcium and protein.
s: Prepare the ingredients: wash and peel the potatoes (800 g). Cut them into very thin slices, about 3 mm, with a well-sharpened knife or a mandoline. Peel the 2 garlic cloves and crush them or chop them very finely. Grate the 150 g of cheese. Grease a heatproof dish of about 20x25 cm with the 20 g of butter.
Turn the oven on to 180°C. Don't rinse the potato slices after cutting, so they keep the starch that thickens the sauce; just pat them dry with a towel.
Arrange a first layer of potato slices in the greased dish, overlapping them slightly. Sprinkle with salt, pepper and a little garlic.
Repeat with a second layer of potatoes, then a third, until you have used all the potatoes and all the garlic. Tip: arrange the layers evenly so they cook evenly.
Pour the 200 ml of cream over the potatoes, so that it seeps between the slices. If it doesn't reach the edges, press the potatoes down lightly with a spoon.
Sprinkle the grated cheese evenly on top. Cover the dish with aluminum foil.
Bake at 180°C for 25 minutes under the foil, then remove the foil and bake for another 15–20 minutes, until the surface turns golden and a knife slides easily into the potatoes.
Take the dish out and let the potatoes rest for 5–10 minutes, so the sauce sets. Serve warm, as a side dish. It keeps in the fridge, covered, for 2–3 days.

12.b: Chicken provides protein, vitamin B12 and niacin.
12.a: Gluten and eggs; the breadcrumbs may also contain soy or sesame.
s: Prepare the ingredients: wash the chicken breast (600 g), dry it well and cut it into slices about 1.5 cm thick, about 4 pieces. Set out three shallow plates: in the first put the 80 g of flour, in the second the 2 eggs beaten with a fork, and in the third the 120 g of breadcrumbs. Get out a large pan and a rack lined with paper towels.

Place the slices between two sheets of plastic wrap and flatten them lightly with a rolling pin or the bottom of a pot, until they are about 1 cm thick all over. Tip: meat of even thickness cooks evenly and stays tender.
Season both sides of the schnitzels with salt and pepper.
Dredge each schnitzel first in the flour, shaking off the excess, then in the egg and finally in the breadcrumbs. Press the breadcrumbs on lightly so they stick over the whole surface.
Heat the 30 ml of oil in a large pan over medium heat. The oil is hot enough when a pinch of breadcrumbs sizzles immediately.
Place the schnitzels in the pan, without crowding them, 2 pieces at a time. Cook them for 4–5 minutes on the first side, until golden.
Turn them with a spatula and cook for another 4–5 minutes, until golden and crisp on both sides. Tip: keep the heat at medium so the breadcrumbs don't burn before the meat is cooked.
Check by cutting into a schnitzel at the thickest point: the meat should be white, with no pink, and the internal temperature should be 75°C. If needed, cook for 1–2 more minutes.
Transfer the schnitzels to paper towels for 1–2 minutes to absorb the fat. Serve hot, with your favorite side dish. They keep in the fridge, in a closed container, for 2 days.

13.b: Protein and iron from the meat, fiber, vitamins and minerals from the vegetables.
13.a: Eggs and celery; the borș and seasonings should be checked for gluten.
s: Prepare the ingredients: peel the carrot (100 g), onion (80 g), celery (80 g) and bell pepper (120 g). Cut them into cubes of about 1 cm. Wash the herbs and chop them finely. Measure out 300 g of ground meat, 50 g of rice, 1 egg, 1.5 l of water and 250 ml of borș. Get out a 3–4 liter pot and a large bowl.
Put the rice in a sieve and rinse it under cold water for 1 minute, then drain it.

In the large bowl, mix the ground meat with the rinsed rice, half of the egg, salt and pepper. Knead by hand for 1–2 minutes, until the mixture holds together. Keep the other half of the egg for thickening.
With wet hands, shape the mixture into meatballs the size of a small walnut, about 3 cm. Place them on a plate. Tip: wet hands keep the meat from sticking to them.

Put the 1.5 l of water in a pot over high heat. Add the onion, carrot, celery and bell pepper and a teaspoon of salt. When the water starts to boil, reduce the heat to medium and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the meatballs to the pot one at a time, carefully, so they don't fall apart. Simmer over low-medium heat for 15–20 minutes, until the meatballs rise to the surface and the meat is no longer pink.
Meanwhile, warm the 250 ml of borș in a small saucepan and boil it for 3–4 minutes, so it doesn't curdle on contact with the soup. Tip: borș added cold or unboiled can make the soup taste too sour.
Beat the other half of the egg with 2–3 tablespoons of warm soup, then pour it in a thin stream into the soup, stirring, to thicken it.
Add the boiled borș to the pot, then the herbs. Taste and adjust the salt and pepper. Leave the soup on the heat for 2 more minutes, then take it off the heat.
Serve hot. It keeps in the fridge, in a closed container, for 3 days.

14.b: Protein from the chicken, fluids for hydration and vitamins from the vegetables.
14.a: Celery, gluten and possibly eggs from the noodles.
s: Prepare the ingredients: wash the chicken (500 g). Peel the carrot (150 g), onion (100 g) and celery (80 g). Cut the carrot into 5 mm rounds, the onion into quarters or large cubes and the celery into 1 cm cubes. Wash the parsley and chop it finely. Measure out 100 g of noodles and 2 l of water. Get out a large 3–4 liter pot.
Put the meat in the pot and cover it with the 2 l of cold water. Place the pot over high heat.

When the water starts to boil, foam and impurities appear on the surface. Skim them off with a slotted spoon for 3–4 minutes, until no more foam forms. Tip: starting with cold water and skimming the foam gives a clear soup.
Reduce the heat to low and add a teaspoon of salt. Simmer the chicken for 20 minutes, with the lid slightly ajar.
Add the onion, carrot and celery to the pot. Simmer for another 30–35 minutes, over low heat, until the vegetables are tender and the meat comes easily off the bone.

Remove the meat with a slotted spoon and put it on a plate. Let it cool for 5 minutes, then pull it off the bones and tear it into small pieces. Check that no pink areas remain; the meat should be white and tender (75°C inside).

Bring the soup back to a boil over medium heat, add the 100 g of noodles and cook them according to the package, about 4–6 minutes, until tender. Tip: if you are making the soup for the next day, cook the noodles separately so they don't absorb the soup.
Put the shredded meat back in the pot and simmer for 1–2 more minutes. Taste and adjust the salt and pepper.
Take the pot off the heat, add the parsley and serve hot. It keeps in the fridge, covered, for 3 days.

15.b: Fiber, vitamin C, potassium and various phytonutrients from the vegetables.
15.a: Celery; check the borș and any seasoning blends.
s: Prepare the vegetables: peel the carrot (150 g), potatoes (250 g), onion (120 g) and celery (80 g), then cut them into 1 cm cubes. Wash the bell pepper (150 g), remove the seeds and cut it into 1 cm cubes. Wash the tomatoes (200 g) and cut them into small cubes. Wash the herbs and chop them finely. Measure out 1.5 l of water, 250 ml of borș and 15 ml of oil. Get out a 3–4 liter pot.
Bring the 1.5 l of water to a boil in a pot over high heat, with a teaspoon of salt.
When the water boils, add the onion, carrot and celery. Simmer over medium heat for 8 minutes.
Add the potatoes and bell pepper and simmer for another 10 minutes, until the potatoes begin to soften.

Add the chopped tomatoes and simmer for another 5–7 minutes, until all the vegetables are tender but not falling apart. Tip: if you want a clearer soup, peel the tomatoes beforehand by blanching them for 1 minute in hot water.

Meanwhile, boil the 250 ml of borș separately in a small saucepan for 3–4 minutes, then pour it into the pot. Boiling it separately keeps the vegetables from curdling and the soup from turning cloudy. Tip: add the borș gradually, tasting, to control the acidity.
Add the 15 ml of oil and the herbs. Taste and adjust the salt, pepper and acidity, adding borș or water as you prefer.
Leave the soup on the heat for 2 more minutes, then take the pot off the heat. Serve hot. It keeps in the fridge, in a closed container, for 3 days.

16.b: Mushrooms provide fiber, B vitamins and minerals.
16.a: Milk; celery if concentrated stock is used. Gluten if thickened with flour.
s: Prepare the ingredients: wipe the mushrooms (400 g) with a damp towel, trim the ends of the stems and cut them into 3–4 mm slices. Peel the onion (100 g) and chop it finely. Peel the potato (150 g) and cut it into 1.5 cm cubes. Peel the garlic and crush or finely chop it. Measure out 15 g of butter, 700 ml of water or stock and 150 ml of cream. Get out a 2–3 liter pot and an immersion blender.
Melt the butter in a pot over medium heat. Add the onion and sauté it for 3–4 minutes, stirring, until translucent.

Add the mushrooms and cook for 6–8 minutes, stirring, until they release their water and then start to brown lightly. Add the garlic and stir for another 30 seconds. Tip: don't crowd the mushrooms, so they brown instead of boiling in their own liquid.
Add the potato, the 700 ml of water or stock, salt and pepper. Raise the heat and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low, partially cover with the lid and simmer for 15 minutes, until the potato is very soft and mashes easily with a fork.
Take the pot off the heat and blend the soup with the immersion blender for 1–2 minutes, until you have a fine, smooth cream. Tip: leave a few whole mushroom slices for garnish and texture.
Put the pot back on low heat and add the 150 ml of cream. Warm it for 2–3 minutes, stirring, without boiling hard, so the cream doesn't curdle.
Taste and adjust the salt and pepper. Serve hot. It keeps in the fridge, in a closed container, for 2–3 days.

17.b: Beans are rich in fiber, plant protein, iron and magnesium.
17.a: Celery; check any seasonings or added products.
s: Prepare the beans the evening before: weigh out 300 g of dried beans, pick them over for impurities, rinse them and put them in a large bowl with cold water, three times their volume. Leave them to soak for 8–12 hours, overnight.

The next day, drain the beans and rinse them. Put them in a 4-liter pot, cover them with 1 liter of cold water and boil them over high heat for 5 minutes. Drain off the water, rinse the beans and put them back in the pot. Tip: the soaking water and the first boiling water are discarded, for easier digestion.
Add the 1.8 l of fresh water. Simmer the beans over low heat, with the lid slightly ajar, for 40–50 minutes, until almost tender and easily squashed between your fingers.
