Meanwhile, prepare the vegetables: peel the carrot (120 g), onion (100 g) and celery (60 g) and cut them into 1 cm cubes. Wash the bell pepper (100 g), remove the seeds and cut it into 1 cm cubes. Wash the tomatoes (150 g) and cut them into small cubes. Chop the herbs.
Add the onion, carrot and celery to the pot, along with 15 ml of oil and a teaspoon of salt. Simmer for 10 minutes.

Add the bell pepper and tomatoes. Simmer for another 10–15 minutes, until the vegetables and beans are completely tender. The beans should be soft, not hard in the middle. Tip: salt added too early can toughen the bean skins.
Taste the soup and adjust the salt and pepper. If it seems too thick, add a little hot water.
Add the herbs, leave it on the heat for 2 more minutes, then take the pot off the heat. Serve hot. It keeps in the fridge, in a closed container, for 3–4 days.

18.b: Vegetables provide fiber and vitamin C; olive oil contains unsaturated fats.
s: Wash the tomatoes (250 g) and cucumbers (200 g). Cut the tomatoes into thick slices or 2–3 cm pieces. Cut the cucumbers into 1 cm rounds, then in half if they are wide. Peel the red onion (40 g) and cut it into very thin rounds. Get out a large bowl.
Cut the 120 g of feta into 1.5–2 cm cubes, or leave it as a whole slice, for serving.
Put the tomatoes, cucumbers and onion in the bowl. Add the 50 g of drained olives. Tip: if the onion is too sharp, soak it in cold water for 5 minutes and drain it.
Add the feta, the 15 ml of olive oil, oregano and a little salt, bearing in mind that the feta and olives are already salty. Toss gently, so the feta doesn't crumble.
Serve immediately, cold. If you won't eat it right away, keep the vegetables and the oil separate and mix just before serving, so they don't release water. It keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

28.b: Tomatoes provide vitamin C and lycopene; olive oil supplies unsaturated fats.
28.a: Gluten from the bread; check the bread for traces of sesame or soy.
s: Prepare the ingredients: preheat the oven to 200°C. Cut the baguette (250 g) into 1.5 cm slices. Wash the tomatoes (250 g), remove the cores and cut them into 1 cm cubes. Peel the garlic clove and cut it in half. Wash the basil (10 g), dry it and tear the leaves. Line a baking tray with baking paper.
Arrange the baguette slices on the tray in a single layer, without overlapping.
Bake at 200°C for 6–8 minutes, turning the slices halfway through, until golden and crisp at the edges.
Take the slices out of the oven and, while they are still warm, gently rub the surface of each one with the cut side of the garlic. Tip: garlic has an intense flavor, so rub only lightly.
In a bowl, mix the tomatoes with the 15 ml of olive oil, the basil, salt and pepper.
Spoon the tomato mixture onto the bread slices just before serving, so the bruschetta stays crisp. Serve immediately.

29.b: Chickpeas provide fiber, plant protein, iron and folate; tahini contains unsaturated fats.
s: Prepare the ingredients: drain the 240 g of cooked chickpeas in a colander. Measure out 40 g of tahini, 30 ml of lemon juice, 30 ml of olive oil and 30 ml of cold water. Peel the garlic clove and cut it in half. Get out a blender or food processor.
Put the chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, half a teaspoon of salt and half of the olive oil into the blender. Tip: if you want a very smooth hummus, peel the skins off the chickpeas.
Blend for 1–2 minutes, stopping once to scrape down the sides of the container with a spatula.
With the blender running, add the water one tablespoon at a time until you reach the desired creamy, smooth consistency. You can use up to 60 ml of water.
Taste and adjust the salt and lemon. Spoon the hummus into a bowl and drizzle with the remaining olive oil. Store in the refrigerator in a closed container for 4–5 days.

i: 20 ml oil for the tray or for frying
30.a: Milk, eggs and gluten; breadcrumbs may contain soy or sesame.
s: Prepare the ingredients: grate or crumble the 200 g of cheese into a large bowl. Measure out 60 g of flour, 80 g of breadcrumbs and 20 ml of oil. Put the breadcrumbs on a plate. Prepare a tray lined with baking paper.
Preheat the oven to 200°C. Add the egg and the flour to the bowl with the cheese.

Mix with a fork or by hand for 1–2 minutes, until you get a smooth, slightly sticky mixture. If it is too soft, add 1 more tablespoon of flour. Tip: let the mixture rest in the refrigerator for 10 minutes so it is easier to work with.
With wet hands, take a spoonful of the mixture at a time and roll it into a 3 cm ball. You will get about 16–20 balls.
Roll each ball in the breadcrumbs, pressing lightly so it is evenly coated.
Place the balls on the tray and lightly brush them with the 20 ml of oil. Bake at 200°C for 15–20 minutes, turning them once, until golden.
Pan-fried variation: heat the oil over medium heat and fry the balls for 4–5 minutes, turning them, until golden. Drain them on paper towels.
Let the balls cool for 3–5 minutes, because the cheese is very hot inside. Serve warm. Store in the refrigerator for 2 days.

31.b: Vegetables provide fiber, vitamins and antioxidants.
31.a: Soy if soy sauce is used; sesame if sesame oil or sauce is added.
s: Prepare the vegetables: wash and peel the carrot (150 g), cabbage (150 g), bell pepper (100 g) and mushrooms (100 g). Cut them into very thin strips, about 3 mm thick and 6–8 cm long. Get out 8 rice paper sheets, a wide dish of lukewarm water, a clean towel and a large frying pan.
Heat the 10 ml of oil in a frying pan over high heat. Add the carrot and cabbage and cook for 2 minutes, stirring.

Add the bell pepper and mushrooms and cook for another 2–3 minutes, stirring, until the vegetables are tender but still crisp. Add salt and, if you like, the gluten-free soy sauce. Let the mixture cool for 5 minutes. Tip: do not overcook the vegetables, or they will turn soft inside the roll.
Soak a rice paper sheet in lukewarm water for 10–20 seconds, according to the package, until it becomes pliable. Lay it on a clean towel.
Place about 3 tablespoons of filling on the lower third of the sheet, leaving a 2 cm border. Tip: do not overfill the sheet, so it does not tear.
Fold the side edges inward, then roll up tightly from the bottom up. Repeat with the remaining sheets, placing the rolls so they do not touch, to keep them from sticking together.

Serve the fresh rolls cut in half. For a browned version, heat a little oil in a frying pan over medium heat and brown the rolls for 2–3 minutes on each side. Store in the refrigerator, covered, for 1 day.

32.b: Tomatoes and bell pepper provide vitamin C; cheese supplies calcium and protein.
32.a: Milk from the cheddar; check the chips and seasonings for soy or traces.
s: Prepare the ingredients: wash the tomatoes (150 g) and the bell pepper (100 g) and peel the onion (50 g). Cut them into very small 5 mm cubes. Grate the 120 g of cheddar. Preheat the oven to 200°C. Get out an ovenproof dish or a tray lined with baking paper.

Put the tomatoes, onion and bell pepper in a bowl. Add the 10 ml of lime juice, salt and pepper and mix. Let the salsa sit for 10 minutes so the flavors come together. Tip: drain off a little of the liquid from the tomatoes so the salsa is not watery.
Arrange half of the 150 g of tortilla chips in the dish in an even layer.
Sprinkle with half of the cheddar. Add the remaining chips and the remaining cheddar.
Bake at 200°C for 5–7 minutes, until the cheddar melts and starts to bubble, without burning the chips. Tip: keep an eye on them, because the chips burn quickly.
Take out the dish and let it rest for 1 minute. Put the salsa on top or alongside and serve immediately, while the cheese is melted.

33.b: Tomatoes contain lycopene; mozzarella contributes protein and calcium.
33.a: Gluten and milk; check the mozzarella and the sauce.
s: Prepare the ingredients: measure out 250 g of flour, 160 ml of lukewarm water (about 35°C), 4 g of dry yeast, 5 ml of oil, 150 g of tomato sauce and 150 g of mozzarella. Cut the mozzarella into thin slices or grate it coarsely. Wash the basil (5 g) and tear the leaves. Get out a large bowl, a baking tray and baking paper.
In a bowl, mix the flour, yeast and a teaspoon of salt. Add the water and oil and stir with a spoon until a dough forms.
Knead the dough on a lightly floured surface for 8–10 minutes, until it is smooth and elastic and no longer sticks to your hands. Tip: if the dough is too sticky, add flour 1 tablespoon at a time.
Shape it into a ball, place it in a bowl lightly greased with oil and cover with a towel. Let the dough rise in a warm place for 45–60 minutes, until it doubles in size.
15 minutes before the end, preheat the oven to 230°C and put the tray inside to heat up.
Put the dough on the floured surface and stretch it by hand or with a rolling pin into a 28–30 cm circle, thicker at the edges. Transfer it to baking paper.
Spread the tomato sauce over the dough, leaving a 1–2 cm border. Add the mozzarella.

Put the pizza (with the paper) on the hot tray and bake at 230°C for 10–15 minutes, until the edges are golden and the mozzarella is melted with golden spots. Tip: baking on a preheated tray makes the crust crispier.
Take out the pizza, sprinkle with the basil and let it rest for 2 minutes. Cut into slices and serve hot. Store in the refrigerator for 2 days.

34.b: Chicken provides protein; mozzarella brings calcium; bell pepper and tomatoes supply vitamins.
34.a: Gluten and milk; check the sauce and seasonings.
s: Prepare the ingredients: measure out 250 g of flour, 160 ml of lukewarm water (35°C), 4 g of yeast, 5 ml of oil, 120 g of tomato sauce and 120 g of mozzarella. Cut the 150 g of cooked chicken breast into strips or 1.5 cm cubes, and the bell pepper (50 g) into thin slices. Grate the mozzarella coarsely. Get out a bowl, a baking tray and baking paper.
In a bowl, mix the flour, yeast and a teaspoon of salt. Add the water and oil and stir until the dough forms.
Knead the dough on a floured surface for 8–10 minutes, until smooth and elastic. Tip: the dough is ready when it springs back slightly after you press it with your finger.
Put the dough in a bowl greased with oil, cover it with a towel and let it rise in a warm place for 45–60 minutes, until it doubles in size.
15 minutes before the end, preheat the oven to 230°C and put the tray inside.
Roll the dough out into a 28–30 cm circle and transfer it to baking paper. Spread it with the tomato sauce, leaving a 1–2 cm border.

Scatter the cooked chicken and the bell pepper over the sauce, then sprinkle the mozzarella evenly. Make sure the chicken is fully cooked, with no pink. Tip: if the chicken is cold, warm it for 1 minute beforehand so it does not cool the pizza.
Bake the pizza (with the paper) on the hot tray at 230°C for 10–15 minutes, until the edges are golden and the mozzarella is melted and lightly browned.
Take out the pizza and let it rest for 2 minutes. Cut into slices and serve hot. Store in the refrigerator for 2 days.

61.n: Peppers Stuffed with Meat and Rice
61.b: Peppers provide vitamin C; meat provides protein and iron.
61.a: No major allergens in the basic ingredients; check the labels of the products you use.
s: Wash the peppers (6 pieces, 600 g), cut off the tops about 1 cm from the stem and carefully remove the cores and seeds. Keep the tops. Peel the onion (100 g) and chop it finely. Chop the parsley. Rinse the rice (80 g). Measure out 400 g of ground meat, 300 g of passata and 30 ml of oil. Prepare a 4–5 liter pot and a large bowl.
Heat the oil in a frying pan and sauté the onion for 3–4 minutes, until translucent. Let it cool for 5 minutes.
In a large bowl, mix the ground meat, rice, sautéed onion, parsley, salt and pepper until the mixture is uniform.

Fill the peppers with the mixture, pressing lightly but without packing it too tightly, because the rice swells as it cooks. Cover each one with its top. Tip: fill the peppers only to 1 cm below the rim.
Stand the peppers upright in the pot, packed tightly next to each other so they do not tip over.
Pour the passata over the peppers, then add water to cover the peppers halfway. Add a little salt.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to low, cover the pot and simmer for 50–60 minutes, until the peppers are tender, the rice is cooked and the meat has no pink left.
Taste the sauce and adjust the salt. Let the peppers rest in the pot for 10 minutes. Serve them warm, with the sauce and, if you like, with bread. Store in the refrigerator for 3 days.

62.b: Lentils are rich in fiber, iron, folate and plant protein.
62.a: No major allergens in the basic ingredients; check the labels of the products you use.
s: Rinse the lentils (250 g) in a sieve under cold running water and check that there are no small stones. Peel the carrots (150 g) and cut them into 5 mm slices. Peel the onion (100 g) and chop it finely. Crush the 3 garlic cloves. Measure out 400 g of diced tomatoes, 5 g of cumin, 15 ml of oil, 1 liter of water and 15 ml of lemon juice. Prepare a 3–4 liter pot.
Heat the oil in the pot over medium heat. Add the onion and carrot and sauté for 4–5 minutes, until softened.
Add the garlic and cumin and stir for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the rinsed lentils, the diced tomatoes, the water and salt. Stir well.

Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to low, partially cover the pot and simmer for 25–30 minutes, until the lentils are tender but do not completely fall apart. Tip: add the salt toward the end if you want more tender lentils.
If the stew is too thick, add a little hot water. Taste a lentil to check that it is tender and adjust the salt and pepper.
Remove from the heat, add the lemon juice and stir. Serve hot, with bread. Store in the refrigerator for 4 days; it can also be frozen.

63.b: Fiber, vitamin C, vitamin A and potassium from the vegetables.
63.a: No major allergens in the basic ingredients; check the labels of the products you use.
s: Wash the vegetables. Peel the potatoes (300 g) and carrots (150 g) and cut them into 2 cm cubes. Cut the zucchini (200 g) and bell peppers (150 g) into 2 cm cubes. Peel the onion (100 g) and chop it finely. Cut the tomatoes (200 g) into cubes. Chop the parsley. Measure out 30 ml of oil. Prepare a 3–4 liter pot or saucepan.
Heat the oil in the pot over medium heat. Add the onion and sauté it for 3–4 minutes, until translucent.
Add the carrot and potatoes and cook for 4–5 minutes, stirring, so they brown lightly.
Add the bell pepper and cook for 2 minutes, stirring.
Add the tomatoes and zucchini, salt and 150 ml of water. Stir. Tip: zucchini cooks quickly, so it is added later.
Bring to a boil, reduce to low, cover and simmer for 25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the potatoes and carrots are tender and the sauce has thickened. Add a little water if it dries out.
Taste and adjust the salt and pepper. Sprinkle with the parsley and serve warm. Store in the refrigerator, in a closed container, for 3 days.

64.b: Beans provide fiber, iron and plant protein.
64.a: No major allergens in the basic ingredients; check the labels of the products you use.
s: If the beans (400 g) were soaked overnight in cold water, drain and rinse them. If not, boil them for 2 minutes and leave them for 1 hour in the hot water. Peel the carrots (150 g) and cut them into 5 mm slices. Peel the onion (150 g) and chop it finely. Crush the 3 garlic cloves. Cut the sausages (300 g) into 1 cm slices. Measure out 15 g of sweet paprika and 30 ml of oil. Prepare a 4–5 liter pot and a frying pan.

Put the beans in the pot with fresh cold water to cover them by 3–4 cm. Bring to a boil, then reduce to low and simmer for 40–50 minutes, until the beans mash easily between your fingers. Drain, keeping 300 ml of the cooking water. Tip: do not salt the beans at the start, so they do not turn tough.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Add the sausages and brown them for 4–5 minutes, until they take on color.
Add the onion and cook for 4–5 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Take the pan off the heat and add the sweet paprika, stirring quickly so it does not burn.
Add the mixture from the pan to the pot with the drained beans. Add the carrot and the reserved cooking water (300 ml).
Simmer on low heat for 15–20 minutes, until the carrot is tender and the sauce has thickened. Taste and adjust the salt and pepper.
Let it rest for 10 minutes and serve hot, with bread. Store in the refrigerator for 3–4 days; it can also be frozen.

65.b: Protein from the chicken and fiber from the vegetables, in a quick meal.
65.a: Contains: Gluten, Milk. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Wash the romaine lettuce (80 g) and the tomatoes (100 g). Drain the lettuce well and cut it into 1 cm strips. Cut the tomatoes into thin slices or small cubes. Cut the cooked chicken (200 g) into strips or small cubes. Crush the garlic clove. Measure out 60 g of yogurt. Prepare a small bowl and a cutting board.
In a small bowl, mix the yogurt with the crushed garlic and a little salt and pepper until smooth.
Warm the tortillas (2 pieces) for 20–30 seconds on each side in a dry frying pan, so they become pliable and do not tear when rolled.
Spread each tortilla with the yogurt sauce, leaving a 2 cm border. Tip: keep a little sauce for serving.
Place the chicken in a strip down the middle of each tortilla, followed by the lettuce and tomatoes.
Fold the side edges inward, then roll up tightly from the bottom up. Cut the wraps in half on the diagonal.
Serve immediately. If you make it ahead, wrap it in foil and keep it in the refrigerator for up to 1 day.

66.b: High in protein, low in fat, with colorful vegetables.
66.a: No major allergens in the basic ingredients; check the labels of the products you use.
s: Wash the chicken breasts (600 g), pat them dry and cut them into 3 cm cubes. Wash the bell pepper (150 g), onion (150 g) and zucchini (150 g) and cut them into 3 cm pieces. Measure out 30 ml of olive oil, 10 g of smoked paprika and 15 ml of lemon juice. If you are using wooden skewers, soak them in water for 20 minutes. Prepare a large bowl and a baking tray.
In a bowl, mix the oil, paprika, lemon juice, salt and pepper. Add the chicken and stir so it is evenly coated.

Cover the bowl and let the chicken marinate for 15–30 minutes in the refrigerator. Meanwhile, preheat the oven to 220°C (or the grill). Tip: if you have more time, marinate the chicken for 2 hours for more flavor.
Thread pieces of chicken, bell pepper, onion and zucchini onto the skewers in alternation, leaving small gaps between them.
Place the skewers on the tray lined with baking paper (or on the grill).
Cook for 15–20 minutes, turning the skewers halfway through, until the chicken is golden and no longer pink in the middle (75°C) and the vegetables are lightly browned.
Let the skewers rest for 3 minutes. Serve them warm, with rice or salad. Store in the refrigerator, in a closed container, for 2 days.

67.b: Protein from the chicken and calcium from the mozzarella.
67.a: Contains: Gluten, Milk. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Cut the bell pepper (60 g) into small 5 mm cubes. Cut the cooked chicken (150 g) into small pieces or thin strips. Grate the mozzarella (120 g). Prepare 2 tortillas, 10 ml of oil, a large frying pan and a spatula.
Lay the tortillas on a cutting board. Sprinkle half of each one with the chicken, bell pepper and mozzarella. Tip: do not add too much filling, so it does not spill out when you flip it.
Fold each tortilla in half over the filling and press down lightly.
Heat half of the oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Add one quesadilla and cook for 3 minutes, until golden on the bottom.
Flip with the spatula and cook for another 3 minutes, until the cheese melts and the tortilla is crisp. Repeat with the second quesadilla.
Transfer to a cutting board, let rest for 1 minute and cut into triangles.
Serve immediately, while the cheese is still stretchy. Store in the refrigerator for 1 day and reheat in a frying pan.

68.b: Eggs provide protein and choline; tomatoes provide lycopene.
68.a: Contains: Eggs. Check the labels of the products you use.
s: Peel the onion (100 g) and chop it finely. Cut the bell pepper (100 g) into 1 cm cubes. Crush the 2 garlic cloves. Chop the parsley. Measure out 400 g of diced tomatoes, 5 g of cumin, 5 g of sweet paprika and 15 ml of oil. Prepare a deep 26–28 cm frying pan with a lid, and 4 eggs.
Heat the oil in the pan over medium heat. Add the onion and bell pepper and cook for 5–6 minutes, stirring, until softened.
Add the garlic, cumin and sweet paprika and cook for 1 minute, stirring, until fragrant. Tip: do not let the spices burn.
Add the diced tomatoes, salt and pepper. Stir and simmer for 10 minutes over low-medium heat, until the sauce thickens.
Make 4 wells in the sauce with the back of a spoon. Crack an egg into each well, carefully, so the yolk does not break.
Cover the pan and cook on low heat for 6–8 minutes, until the whites are completely set and opaque and the yolks are the way you like them (runny or firmer). Tip: for a firm yolk, cook for 8 minutes.
Sprinkle with the parsley and serve immediately, straight from the pan, with bread. Best eaten fresh.
